Title: 40F. Uninsured. Botched surgery. Hospital wants out. Looking for help.
Body:
My cousin (40sF) in Florida is uninsured and called 911 after passing out at home. She was found to have internal bleeding from a newly discovered tumor and needed a hysterectomy. After the surgery she wasn't voiding and had signs of infection so they took her for another exploratory surgery. It was found that the OB/GYN who performed the hysterectomy also severed both ureters causing peritonitis. The surgeon placed a urostomy and a JP drain. She has been in the hospital for about a month now and is significantly debilitated from it: barely able to walk to the bathroom, etc. She admittedly doesn't have a significant drive to get better as evidence by refusing PT several times for not feeling well.

Now the advice part. She still needs another surgery to reverse her stoma and repair her ureters. The surgeon has told her he's arranged for a urologist friend at another hospital to do the surgery free of charge. The catch is she has to be discharged from the current hospital and walk into the other hospital through the ED. This is setting off so many red flags for me. Can a surgeon just do a surgery pro bono? What about the anesthesia side of it, the medications, and the hospital stay? The fact that they won't transfer her is making me feel like they just want to wipe their hands clean.  I would speculate it's because she's uninsured and she's been there for a month, but who knows. 

To me, if she's medically cleared I feel like it is better to be discharged to rehab, gain strength, allow her insides to heal from the 2 surgeries, and then figure out reversing the stoma later. Stoma reversal doesn't seem urgent, but I'm getting all information through her and it seems like she doesn't fully grasp on every detail. If she does need another surgery more urgently I feel like it should be done at the current hospital (they should fix their own mistake) or allow her a direct transfer to the other specialist. Under no circumstances does being discharged to the street and walking into the other ED seem like a good idea but I'm happy to be told otherwise. I'm an ICU RN so I want to help but I feel like she needs a combination of medical, administrative, and legal advice. And help is much appreciated.
Response:
I think you're feeling that this is fishy because it very much is. This shit reeks of malpractice to me. There'd better not be any bill associated with the complications resulting from severing her ureters and not even noticing until she almost dies, which goes beyond the usual and expected risks associated with surgery.

I don't have much to offer, but I do want to point out that if they're telling her to be discharged and walk into a different hospital's ER for care, that's a violation of the federal EMTALA law called "patient dumping". It carries a significant fine of up to $50,000 for the offending hospital. That they're even suggesting such a thing is wrong. If there's truly a surgeon willing to do this pro bono, she'd better get it in writing. And there would be absolutely no reason she would need to go through the ER if this were legit, because this would be a scheduled inpatient procedure.

Additionally, she's going to have a difficult time finding a surgeon who is willing to perform surgery after a different surgeon has already carved up the same area. Even more difficulty if she tries to pursue it on her own. Surgeons don't like to be stuck with a different surgeon's mess, because as soon as they do anything the responsibility becomes theirs.

Title: Anxiety attacks brought on by sound? 28, F, 5’4, 110lbs, ongoing issue, no current medical problems or medications
Body:
I know this sounds crazy but for the longest time I have always had an issue with sounds. For example, I cannot stand the sound of another person eating near me. It makes me feel like I’m going to explode inside and I get really irritable. It’s affecting my home life but it’s uncontrollable. The same thing happens when I hear pencils writing on paper. Also when there is too much noise in one place (tv on, music in background, kids on phone..all at one time) I have full blown anxiety attacks and have to leave. Is something wrong with me? I feel like I should just be able to stop myself from getting so irritated but it’s like instant and uncontrollable irritation as soon as I’m in any of these situations. 

I am a healthy 28yo F with no medical issues. 5’4, 110lbs, ongoing issue for as long as I can remember but seems to be getting worse.
Response: You're not alone, and this happens enough that there's a term for it, misophonia, although it's not a standardized diagnosis. There's also little clear guidance on what to do about it. It's possible that therapy, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy, can help you manage the overwhelming reaction, but nobody really knows.

Title: Guillemot-Barre and COVID vaccine?
Body:
I had Guillan-Barre from a flu shot about 5 years ago, at the time I was told to never get a vaccine again. At the beginning of COVID my VA physician told me to not get the vaccine. I’ve done a little bit of my own research and have seen that the CDC states no correlation between GB and the vaccine. What is the consensus here and do y’all think it is safe?

26M, 5’10”, 225, multiple psychiatric medications, non-smoker
Response:
Your chances of GBS and/or death are substantially higher with Covid-19 than with the vaccine.

That said, I'd advise getting one of the mRNA vaccines as less likely to cause a problem, because there are fewer ingredients and the ingredients are simpler than the older technology vaccines.

Also, having a history of GBS means that in the unlikely event that it happens to you again after a virus or vaccine exposure, you can recognize it and get treated asap.

Title: 68 year old mother fell in middle of night and found in pool of blood with her skull cracked open
Body:
It has been about 40 hours since my mom was found in a pool of blood after what we assume is her fainting in the middle of the night and struggling to get someone upstairs attention unsuccessfully. (this happened about 10 years ago but not as severe, my sister heard her and she just needed a few stitches and was sent home) 

We don’t know how long my mom was laying there in that state as it could have happened anytime between 12am and 530am, but when my father found her unconscious and full of blood called 911 and followed their instructions to ensure she was still breathing. She suffered brain hemmorages and had to get surgery that we’d be told may come with deficits. Surgery went well thank the lord and we are being told the part of the brain that’s effected will be the use of her left arm and leg, her skull is still open to ensure any swelling that may occur will not be met with pressure against the skull. The doctor said the next 4 days are crucial and so far she’s been stable. 

My mother had neck and head scans today and we were told the results are good. The doctors were surprised as although she is currently in an induced coma she is starting to move her left leg and arm. I understand the docs can’t say anything reassuring at this point as it is wayyy to early but they did say she’s doing good based on the situation. 

Although I have a million questions running through my head at once my main one is: when she manages to pull through is there a chance she can become her old self or do these injuries always change the person? 

My mom is such a selfless loving woman it broke my heart that in the morning of my nephews baptism and the whole house dressed for the event my mother struggled alone and almost died for what could be hours.
Response:
Too many subtleties to head injuries in the elderly.

You need to ask her doctors who know what’s going on , nobody here will be able you give you a good answer,  we’d just be guessing

Title: MALE, 21: My psych is an NP and told me Adderall and SSRI's don't interact. Is it wrong to question her judgement on my meds?
Body:
I had a licensed doctor as my psychiatrist and prescriber for over a year and he was great, well he moved and the clinic moved all his patients to a Advanced Nurse Practitioner. I'm taking Sertraline 150mg and Adderall XR 15mg every day. 

I'm starting to doubt her judgement on the topic of my medication, as nice as she is it seems like she doesn't know a lot about medication. I'm not even a doctor and I know Adderall is related to serotonin and that these two meds interact. 

I mean, I know it's the internet but drugs.com even says they interact and should be avoided being taken in combination. 

She's done this in the past. She wanted to switch my SSRI to Wellbutrin along side the Adderall I already take. I didn't feel comfortable doing that, I brought these concerns up to her and she told me these meds don't interact which is absolutely false, right?

Would it be wrong to seek out another doctor? Or tell her that she's wrong? 

Or am I wrong?
Response: Many medications have the possibility of having negative interactions. That possibility does exist for Adderall and SSRIs when used together. However, that doesn't preclude them being used together, and they're quite frequently prescribed together to patients given that people know what to look out for in terms of side effects. I take care of multiple patients who take SSRIs and Adderall and are doing just fine.

Title: Lack of vitamins causing high heart rate & shortness of breath while jogging?
Body:

I got my blood work done earlier this month and my Vit B12 level is 167 pg/ml (normal levels 187-883) and Vit D level is 7.6 ng/ML (normal levels 30 to 100). I am deficient in both the vitamins and I'm currently on supplements.

Whenever I am on a morning walk and do a small jog, like 20-25 seconds, I am out of breath and my heart rate increases. My avg. heart rate during my walks are between 125-135 bpm but whenever I jog it shoots up to 160-170 and causes me to panic/get an anxiety attack.

Title: Doctors don't take me seriously because I'm young so I'm going to ask for opinions here. It's a heart issue. I'd really like some thoughts on what's going on.
Body:
So I doubt many people, if any, will read all of this but I'm going to leave it here just in case because I'm at loss. 

To preface: I'm a 20 year old female of healthy weight (BMI of 19.8) and I exercise 3-5 days a week. Particularly, I jog or walk. On days where I can't run/jog I walk for an hour or two. On days where standing and walking is tolerable, I jog and take walk breaks as needed (I can't jog for more than a minute at a time because of my heart rate reaching it's maximum quickly). Been doing this for about a year. I drink a lot of water and I typically get around 7-9 hours of sleep a night. My blood pressure tends to sit around 105/75. I have no mineral or vitamin deficiencies, thyroid issues, etc (I get them routinely checked). The only weird thing is I've had a consistently elevated sedimentation rate for a while. I have a whole host of other problems (hands, feet, flu-like feelings on and off for the past year, chronic fatigue, endometriosis, severe bloating, episodes that are suspected to be seizures, and a couple other things) so it could be something to do with that. 

Basically, I have problems with a racing, pounding heart as well as shortness of breath, light headedness, and pressure in my chest. The thing I use to check my HR is my fitness watch. I've tested it against other devices and counted manually to check its accuracy, and it's very accurate, give or take a couple of points sometimes. 

Some days it's worse than others. I'm going to stand up and just describe what happens as my symptom occur. 

I just stood up, and I feel like I'm not getting enough oxygen, and there's a burning feeling in my muscles kind of. Similar to the sensation one gets after stopping and standing after having been running for a while; feeling winded. My heart rate is 134 as of about 20 seconds. I really feel a need to hunch over or sit or lie down. I feel a heaviness and pressure in my chest. My heart is beating fast and hard.

As of a minute, my heart rate is 150. I keep taking a sudden deep breath every so often because the air hunger won't go away. It's very difficult to stand up straight right now. The area below my breast bone, in the center, is pulsating hard too and I can see it if I look there. Every fiber of me is filled with fatigue and just standing feels laborious. 

 It's been around 4 minutes now and it's somewhat less intense, my heart rate is 137. I still feel the heaviness and air hunger. I feel so, so tired physically and want to collapse into bed.. I'm going to lay down, I can't stand it anymore. My heart beat really hard and slow for a few seconds after laying down, and I feel immense relief as the air hunger and urge to lay down is releasing and fading away. My heart rate is now at 83. 

Some other info:

When I jog, after about a minute my heart rate is between 170-180, even if it's a light jog. Then I take a walk break. Then, after that, my heart will reach 200 every time unless I watch it very carefully. A couple times, it went to 203. I try to check a lot and try to not let it go over 190. Today is a fairly bad day, so even walking is too much for me. Just going upstairs will send my heart rate up to the 150s today, sometimes as much as 180 and it feels so unpleasant and laborious to do. Bending over to pick things up and just being up and about on my feet in general feels laborious and difficult physically. 

Last week.. I had a normal day. It rarely happens, but it does. Going up flights of stairs was easy and my hr barely exceeded 100. When standing it stayed between 80-100, even walking didn't send it over 110 really. So I decided to go for a run.. and it all got messed up :( for the rest of the day after my run, my resting heart rate rarely would dip below 90-100 let alone walking around. 
I also have some days where while I don't feel good, I'm able to get myself to outside and alternative between walking and jogging for at least 30 minutes to an hour. It's really hard but I'm trying. 

Something really strange is caffeine lowers my heart rate, and you'd think it would raise it. When I go to work, if I'm having a bad day with my heart caffeine grounds me, reduces my heart rate and lightheadedness. It doesn't always help with the pounding though, my heart rate may be lower but often it'll still beat hard. 

 I did a 30 day heart monitor - no detected arrhythmias. 

I just wish I could snap my fingers and make this go away. I wish it wasn't so expensive to try to get this all checked out, and that I didn't have to go through more than one doctor to find someone who would take me seriously and look into my issue instead of telling me to drink more water and eat more salt and send me on my way (I got news for them: it doesn't make a difference no matter how much water I drink). Anyone have any ideas on what might likely be happening? My mental health is starting to decline and I'm just not happy anymore. I want to be able to be active and feel at least decent every day but I never feel good. And it's too expensive to get to the bottom of this. I don't know why to do anymore and don't know how my body is going to go decades like this, there's no way I won't have issues or complications when I age from this. I don't want to spend my life barely being able to stand some days, it feels so unfair because I try to exercise and eat well and stay hydrated but nothing works. I'm just tired, and sick of this. 

That was super long, I know. Thoughts?
Response:
Can you clarify a few things—
When you had your 30 day monitor did you have any fast heart rates noted on there? Did you push yourself to reproduce those events while on monitor? 
Have you had orthostatic blood pressures? If so, what was your BP and HR?
Do you feel well hydrated? Is your urine dark, yellow, light, or clear? 
Did you have these symptoms prior to starting Adderall? 
Do you warm up before exercising? Does a long warm up help your HR? 
Did you have basic lab work? If so, What was your hemoglobin and hematocrit?

Title: Was my pregnancy high-risk?
Body: My husband who is an EM physician doesn’t seem to think it was. Let me tell you why I think it was. 34y.o./first pregnancy/ normal weight/ normal height/ No prior health conditions. At our 20 week ultrasound they determined I had placenta previa. They also found that our daughter had potential hydro nephrosis in one kidney which required 2 additional in-depth ultrasounds. And an ultrasound once she was born to be sure her kidneys were fine. My placenta previa required ultrasounds every 6 weeks and though it moved, it didn’t move enough, which resulted in a planned c-section at 39 weeks. Once diagnosed with PP, I was put on modified “couch rest” for the duration of my pregnancy and couldn’t exercise, have sex, etc. The day before my c-section, I tested postive for covid, so covid precautions were taken during surgery/recovery and the duration of our hospital stay. Baby roomed in with us. Baby’s kidneys were fine and she tested negative for covid at 24 and 48 hours, Thank God. I don’t tell people I had a high risk pregnancy but it came up in conversation with my husband and I told him I was definitely high risk. He disagreed. Help me settle this disagreement. TIA
Response: Yes, definitely high risk. Placenta previa and low lying placentas have a significant risk of hemorrhage if a patient labors.

Title: 28f post miscarriage looking for layman’s explanation of doctor summary.
Body:
28f . Just had a twin miscarriage. Suspected possible bicornuate uterus. No medications, non-smoker. Just received doctors summary from imaging of uterus taken today and looking for an easier to understand translation.

Cervix was cannulated with standard aseptic technique, noting need to use sound,
and injection carried out without difficulty. Patient is undergone cesarean
section and 1 miscarriage. She is suspected to have a bicornuate uterus

Bicornuate uterus is present. The left side shows normal endometrial cavity,
prompt flow out normal appearing fallopian tube and free spill. The right side
shows a blunted and slightly distended cornu, probably postoperative scar. There
was no flow out the right-sided tube, with continuous low anterior intermittent
pressure. Patient tolerated procedure well
Response:
Not a doctor. At all. But human anatomy is a subject I have studied extensively. So, while we wait for a better-credentialed user to respond or refute, here's my offering. 

I am going to assume you know what the anatomy is for terms like "cervix" and "uterus" and "fallopian tube"?

A "bicornate" uterus is shaped like a heart (bi = two and cornate = horn, in the Latin) instead of just a nice round thing. A malformed uterus like this is associated with stuff like worse reproductive outcomes like preterm labor.

Take a look here: 

To be "cannulated" means to have a tube inserted into... They stuck a tube into your cervix with "aseptic" technique, which means "without infection" (a- = without, -septic = infection).

In the end, they did the stuff to test for your suspected uterine malformation and it appears to be present, per this report. Further investigations show that the RIGHT side, especially the fallopian tube, don't quite work right. The fallopian tube carries eggs from the ovary to the uterus and this one looks like it no work too good?

In layman's terms, your uterus almost wants to be two different ones but instead became heart-shaped and the right side, including the fallopian tube, don't quite work right for whatever reason.

Here is an article that seems pretty digestible: 

You've also had some surgery in this anatomical area which may have resulted in some scarring that "distended", or stretched the "cornu" which is just the medical term for a specific part of the uterus.

I don't know what this means for you in your particular case, but am happy to apply what little knowledge I possess to ease and embolden whatever legwork you do to inform yourself of your health.

Thank you for seeking information about your body in a way that is meaningful and understandable to you.

Title: Pregnant with a Skyla IUD that is not expelled, question?!
Body:
My 17 year old is super responsible. She talked to me about having sex in advance, and we went to the doctor right away and she started birth control pills.  After experiencing some issues with mood due to the hormones, she was switched to another pill but still had a bad experience. Gyn recommended Skyla IUD (99.4% effective).  My daughter had the IUD inserted 4 months ago, and we just learned that she is 7 weeks pregnant!

I've been researching this online and it seems that pregnancy is a "rare" occurrence, but discusses serious issues that can be caused when a pregnacy occurs with an IUD in place such as septicemia.  We are planning to terminate the pregnancy, but since we live in Texas, there are not a lot of places to do this so it will take another 2 weeks before she has her appointment.  In the meantime, should I be worried about other serious complications?  My daughter did have the first appointment consultation that included an ultrasound last week, and they did not say anything about an ectopic pregnancy, so I'm assuming that will not be an issue. 

I just want to know how worried I should be while we are waiting to have the IUD removed?
Response:
The biggest concern would be that the pregnancy is ectopic. I would confirm that the ultrasound showed an intrauterine pregnancy.

Besides that, not much concern about a pregnancy with IUD in place - if people choose to continue the pregnancy to term in some cases they leave the IUD in until delivery.

Thanks for being an open and supportive parent.

Title: Surgery Esphyixiation
Body:
Age 32

Sex M

Height 5'9"

Weight 260

Race Black 
 
My husband had surgery Friday morning at UPenn in Pennsylvania. He has a restriction in his urethra, so they wanted to put in a suberpubic Catheter tube in for 3 weeks to give his urethra a break before they go in and fix the restriction.

So when I went to meet him his face was splotchy and eyes were red and bulged, lips were dark. I asked what happened and he said he didn't know but they had him exhaling through this breathing thing to make sure his oxygen levels were OK. No one at the hospital said anything. 

We left but he was light headed and really disoriented at home. He had trouble doing simple things like using the microwave. So we went to emergency and they said he looked like he had symptoms of choking or asphyixiation. But that there was nothing in his notes from the surgery saying what happened to him. 

We've been to the emergency twice and there's no underlying issues with him, so it was something that happened during surgery, but no one is giving us any answers. 

I'm not even sure what to really ask here, but we just don't know what could have happened to him.
Any suggestions would be great as well as some pain relief 


[Husband'seyes](
Response:
This is a scary looking but benign issue. Typically patients are placed in a legs up - head down position for cystoscopy for suprapubic catheter insertion. The combination of IV fluid given during the procedure and the irrigation fluid used to fill the bladder up during the procedure (to bring the bladder wall next to the skin, to allow suprapubic catheterization) will often lead to temporary swelling (edema) due to the fluid given. This is particularly common in procedures using a head-down position and also in prolonged procedures. The conjunctival hemorrhage and edema looks alarming but is harmless and will resolve on its own without treatment. 

The breathing device you refer to is possibly a nebulizer given to improve oxygenation of the lungs after surgery. This is likely simply standard postoperative treatment in a patient whose obesity reduces oxygenation (which is also ordinarily reduced in the initial postoperative phase.)

Title: How painful is sudden cardiac arrest?
Body:
For reference, my late father (58M) was Caucasian, 6’0, roughly 180lbs-200lbs, had high cholesterol, and a hernia in lower stomach. 

•His diet wasn’t exactly the best (mostly red meat, potatoes, and dairy on a regular basis). 


•Wasn’t on any medications, was a smoker for several years but quit over two decades ago. 


•Had Covid-19 in July 2020, which he recovered from after a week and a half with no medical treatment 


•No other known health issues except that heart problems does run on his side of the family. He passed away due to sudden cardiac arrest late last month. 

He was perfectly fine that morning the day he died and him and his coworkers were having a beer at lunch (which was unusual in itself, since my dad doesn’t really drink). A few hours later, he started feeling violently ill very quickly (nausea, vomiting, profuse sweating, blue-tinted lips, pale clammy skin). He lost consciousness at work and his coworker performed CPR on him until the ambulance came. He died shortly after at the hospital after a half hour of resuscitation attempts. 

I vaguely remember my dad telling my mom in the kitchen one day that he was experiencing chest pains and back pain, which he thought nothing of. Were these possible warning signs of cardiac arrest? 

All I can think about is how long my dad suffered for before he died. Is sudden cardiac arrest a slow and agonizing way to die? Or is it quick and painless once one loses consciousness?
Response:
Typically, sudden cardiac arrest is not painful. It is rather quick. There is no prolonged suffering like dying from a long-term disease. If it provides any solace, your father likely felty dizzy then lost consciousness. Once you lose consciousness, there is no pain.

I am sorry for your loss. Don't feel selfish to seek help from a health counselor/therapist who can provide grief support as you honor your father's life.

Title: What happened to my mom?
Body:
My mom (55) has been feeling off since almost 1.5 years. On a tuesday morning in February 2020, she started the day off with a headache that lasted two days. During those two days, her blood pressure spiked to 175/95, which prompted us to take her to our GP. He did a blood test, but the results showed nothing out of the ordinary. She has had high blood pressure for more than 20 years, taking daily medication, so the GP told her that there's nothing wrong.

  


In the following month, she measured her blood pressure every day and noted her results, which is what the GP asked for. Her blood pressure swung between 120-180 systolic 75-90 diastolic. More worryingly however, is that she has had numerous new symptoms since then. These have been more serious during the early phase (Feb to July 2020), but these still affect her almost daily even today:

  


1.  Struggling with spatial awareness. She has trouble sensing where people and objects were, not knowing when someone wants to pass or that a hot stove is melting the plastic near it.
2.  Trouble with vision. In April 2020, she did an eye test. However, she couldn't mention any letters. According to her, she saw the letters clearly, but couldn't convert that to pronouncing a letter. It just didn't "click".
3.  Forgetting everyday things. Even though she has walked from our supermarket to our home hundreds of times, instead of a quick 15 minutes travel, it takes her an hour now. She has forgotten recipes of foods that she has made thousands of times.
4.  Slower thinking/acting. Her brain just seems slower. She takes more time for walking, getting something, thinking of a word, of recipes, everything. This isn't the regular descent of speed due to age, it has been an instant change ever since that February morning. According to her, she feels "slow".
5.  Merging of colors. She thinks that some foods are others, as they're the same color. Certainly the most minor point.

  


Is there a condition or reason that could be tied to all of this? The most likely reasons are age, weight gain and covid depression I think, but she seems like a different person compared to two years ago. She doesn't feel well and we are planning to go to a neurologist when she has gotten her vaccines, hoping that that might clear things up.
Response: OP your mom needs evaluation from a neurologist as soon as you can get her seen

Title: Sweating profusely, testicular pain, chills and acting strange.
Body:
My husband is a 28 year old caucasian. He is 5'11" and weighs roughly 180lbs give or take a few. He has no known medical conditions and no family history of mental illness. The only prescription drugs he is currently taking is Doxycycline (detailed below). He smokes marijuana daily and uses and e-smoke with 4mg nicotene. 

About 2 weeks ago he began sweating profusely, having chills, complaining about on and off testicular pain (like being kicked, painful for a short time and gradually going away) and wasnt feeling well in general. Then things got really weird. It was like he became a totally different person, he was confused, he stayed up all night with no sleep, he was talking crazy incoherent talk, and I was eventually forced to take him to our local ER due to his behavior. He would not cooperate with the staff and was given 2 injections of Haldol (possibly some other things as well). They did urine tests and bloodwork. The next day when he woke up he didnt remember anything and was his normal self. He was cleared by our local mental health team. Our family doctor came by and explained that the urine tests showed something and it could possibly be caused by some E.coli bacteria that had gotten into the tube behind the testicles and that combined with smoking pot could have caused the strange episode. He was prescribed a 7 day cycle of Doxycycline to clear up the infection and we went home. 

Things were great for about a week, he stopped smoking weed until he was done the antibiotics and I thought things were going back to normal. About four days ago the symptoms returned, sweating all the time in excessive amounts, chills, pain in the testicles, ect. I made him an appt with our family doc and again we did urine and bloodwork. We also got a chest xray done and were told we would have the results on this upcoming Monday Feb 26th. At this time we are awaiting a call from the CT/Ultrasound department to have an ultrasound done on the kidneys and testicals. We also discovered that the testicular pain seemed to occur in the right side specifically and not directly in the testicle but in behind them? He was offered another antibiotic prescription but my husband refused thinking it would be useless. Things were fine for a few hours until he started the crazy talk again. I took him back to the ER but this time he was cooperative (not as "far gone" as the first incident).

The doctor ordered another urine test and prescribed him a 3 day cycle of Doxycycline and sent us home. My husband told me he was tired and wanted to sleep so we went to bed early. Like the time before he stayed awake the whole time and didn't sleep. He woke me up at 2:00AM with his crazy talk and kept getting louder and at 3:00AM I took him back to the ER. He was given another Haldol injection and we waited until 6:00AM when the doctor assessed him. She ordered a CT scan for his head and we are now waiting on that (along with the aforementioned ultrasounds). I asked if we could get something to help him sleep since last time when he slept he woke up feeling like himself. She gave him a 1mg ativan and sent us home.

This morning he woke up a bit better but remembered everything. He is still not himself and I dont know what to do. He sweats like mad and babbles and it seems like the doctors can't do anything until we get the CT and ultrasounds done. He is a bit more coherent than before but still goes off about how he feels possessed and thinks he is the only thing that exists. I am looking for any advice anyone might have. Anything I could suggest to the doctors or if anyone has seen something like this before please. This is so unlike him, we have been together for 4 years and I've never seen anything like this from him. I need help.
Response: I’m sorry you guys are going through this. I know this can be difficult. Sounds like your doctors are doing an appropriate work up for altered mental status. The best course of action is to wait for the results. Continue to abstain from alcohol and marijuana and any other substances that can have neurological effects. Marijuana can be associated psychosis is some individuals. Does he have a fever ( temp above 100.5 F)? What country do you live in? Any international travel? Any odd or unique hobbies or jobs?

Title: Why are patients not sedated during IUD insertion?

Why is this not a practice in the US? 

I would do it again because I think its worth it, but dear lord I feel like I have PTSD. I shudder when I think about how bad it was.
Response:
So for some people I offer a paracervical local anesthetic block. This mostly numbs the cervix. It may offer some uterine numbing, too.

Also for people with extreme pain or anxiety I will have them come in an hour early, sign consents, then have them pop a Xanax and a Percocet and weeeeeeeeee off we go to a new iud without much issue.

I offer the same for colposcopies if people are very worried. 

Otherwise if people seem chill I do not mention it as nothing is without risk.

Title: How much sertraline does it take to overdose
Body:
Male 120lb 5ft 4in no drugs no smoking no other meds

I have a depressed roommate and I'm holding onto his antidepressants for him, giving him a pill every morning (his request). He is now wanting a larger dose so he doesn't have to keep asking every day (ex. Suggests I give him a week's worth at a time) but he has severe thoughts of overdosing and I don't want to give him a lethal amount in case he gives in.

What do you recommend for a safe amount? Or to be cautious should I say No, and keep giving it daily?
Response:
This is a complex situation.

Firstly, no one can adequately risk assess someone based on several lines of information. The most conservative and safest option forward would obviously be to provide him one day at a time.

Secondly, are you, as his 'roommate', prepared and are you the right person to be taking on this much responsibility over his safety? 

Thirdly, if his risk is high enough to warrant a friend keeping his medications for him and administering it daily, should he not be accessing a higher level of medical attention than he is currently receiving?

Fourthly, if he is truly and severely suicidal, keeping his medications stashed away wouldn't be enough; if someone is determined to take their own life out in the community, they will find a way. Should he be admitted into a psychiatric hospital?

These are just some quick questions that popped into my mind reading your post. There is probably more that would need to be considered to manage the situation safely. Please ensure your roommate is engaging with his psychiatric team and, if you decide you wish to take on this responsibility, that they are liaising with you so that you're working cohesively.

Title: A Mystery In My Knee. A Mystery I Can’t See.
Body:
Hello Everyone,

I’m 18M and Athlete. 

I’ll preface this by saying that I’m really scared. Not because of the my knee itself, but rather the fact that nothing that I find online, through my doctor, and a specialist, align with what’s wrong with my knee. 

In regards to what happened to my knee: I was running (or sprinting, I should say) on gym flooring, and had stepped on my shoelace. This had caused me to fall directly on the top-right half of the left knee (inside facing), which had then swelled up in less than 20 seconds and caused me to be in an immobilized and painful state. I took two ibuprofens and went to sleep, and in a week, the swelling was greatly reduced and I could walk/run/perform as I did before. Keep in mind that the swelling was more of that of a bruise, and character of the bruise was that of a vertical line going up from the point of impact, to mid thigh. 

Three weeks after, I was walking and suddenly my knee gave way for a second, it felt like a tear or a snap, and from then on I have had this weird  feeling of instability and my knee “not feeling right”. After two weeks of this dull yet aching pain, I see the doctor and she recommends an X-ray. I take it, and it turns out that nothing is found to be “wrong” with the bones. 

Countless hours of YouTube videos, online research, RICE, topical ointments, and patience later, I realize that none of my symptoms are lining up with a pinpoint answer on what’s wrong with me. So I come to r/AskDocs so that you may offer some enlightenment. 

My symptoms include:
- Feeling of instability in the knee joint
- The need to constantly crack my knee in order to release a feeling of pressure
- Dull and/or irritable pain after exercise
- Constant cracking/releasing of air, which gives relief 
- Discomfort when wearing knee brace
- Feel as though the knee joint is “rough”

[Both knees are identical, no swelling or tenderness, am able to manipulate the knee in its natural range of motion without pain or discomfort, can twist and turn the knee without pain, can walk/sit/run normally without pain, no other history of knee problems/injuries]

My best guess(es) on what’s wrong with me:
- Articular Cartilage damage
- Knee/Ligament sprain

*Due to very extraneous circumstances, I am unable to get an MRI, I may however get an ultrasound potentially, if the stars become aligned*

If I’m lucky enough to get engagement from you guys, I would be very relieved and grateful. My fear stems from how this may impact my line of work (National Defence) and wether or not this may be something serious. 

Thank you, for taking the time to read this.
Response: I'll make this quick. You need an MRI and nothing else is going to give you the answer you want. You can see an orthopod who can do a physical exam to get a sense of what is wrong. But the degree of severity is likely going to be imaging dependent.

Title: Can you really retrain your brain after severe psychological trauma at a young age and witnessing a traumatic death. Can I ever live a normal life? Please help me.
Body:
Hello 

F 22, healthy BMI, diagnosed with depression, PTSD and borderline personality disorder.

Can you really retrain your brain after living through complex trauma? I lived through quite heavy psychological trauma, at ages 11-15 years old. I am now 22 years old and my responses to almost all normal situations are faulty. Everything I do currently, the way I think, act, feel and even behave are faulty and impacted by my past. It's as if my brain has not and cannot recognise that I am in a different situation right now. All my coping mechanisms are also flawed.

I am asking about the brains capacity to regenerate and adapt - **is this really possible if trauma was at such a young age?** Things like abandonment - perceived or real, is just one of the things that dictates my whole life now. This causes me so much unhappiness, I feel trapped. No matter how many times I tell myself that things are different now, it's like my brain can't catch up with me and is still stuck in the past. 

**Will I ever be able to live a normal life? Do people recover from things like this, or can I expect to live in this state for the rest of my life?**

I hope this question is in the right place, thank you.
Response:
The brain is remarkably adaptable, and so are our emotions. In the same way that trauma can re-shape your experiences and reactions in a bad way, some dedicated work can re-train those pathways and help you lead a more fufilling life. There are a *lot* of options available to you. This is going to be sort of a pro/con. On one hand, the choices can seem overwhelming and, unfortunately, the burden is on you to find the right "fit." Hard to want to do that when you're already suffering, but it will be so worth it. EMDR, if it is available in your area has shown great promise in helping people recover from trauma. A good google search will probably give you better info that I could, although a couple of my colleagues are trained in EMDR, I am not and have little exposure to it because it doesn't fit what I'm doing right now. I've heard remarkable success stories though. If that's not available, which is very possible, I would seek a psychologist who lists CBT and Trauma both as specialties. CBT is going to be the crux of any effective therapy you do, even EMDR. The process of treatment will be retraining your emotional responses to external stimuli. It's hard work in the sense that it's uncomfortable (and it will be), but it's not any more taxing that learning any new skill. Have patience with the process. It's ok to be mad at your shrink for making you feel bad, as long as you process that with them and it leads to growth. It's not good if they're just a jerk, but lordy I hope that isn't the case.

Having said all that,  it's easy to think of what you want to do as breaking an old, bad habit. It's going to take some time and dedication. You'll slip along the way. But eventually you can break it, if you stick with it.  Good luck!

Title: Help interpreting blood test
Body:
27M here. I was told I was slightly anemic about 1.5yrs ago. They haven’t identified the cause yet but initially my iron saturation was low. I just got my latest blood test results and hepatic panel and Now I’m confused. All of my iron and ferritin results are normal now. But the below results were abnormal.

wbc: 3.4 (4.5-11) Rbc: 4.4 (4.5-5.9) Hgb: 13.2 (13.5-17.5) Alkaline phosphatase 30 ( 40-140)

Everything else was in the normal range. I guess my questions are:

1.	⁠what would cause my wbc count to be low? During my previous 3 tests over the last year the count was always normal between 5-6.5.
2.	⁠same question for the alkaline phosphatase. Everything I’ve seen online says it’s an issue when it’s high but there not much about the cause of it being low.
3.	⁠if my iron studies were all normal yet my RBC and HGB is still low, what anemia would that be then?

Thanks for any help, this has been weighing on my mind while I wait to hear from the doctor.
Response:
1. WBC can be low for many reasons: bone marrow suppression from toxins (e.g. alcohol, medications), acute illness (e.g. viral syndromes, sepsis) or more rarely bone marrow processes (leukemias, myelodysplastic syndromes, generally bad stuff). In all comers, the last group is much less likely to be the culprit than the first two, just in case you're getting worried.
2. Alk phos being low is generally not something to worry about. On medicine board tests they love to mention the association of low alk phos with Wilson's disease, but that is not the cause in the vast majority of people. Zinc and magnesium levels seem to correlate with alk phos, but not in any way that should affect management decisions to my knowledge. Low bone turnover (bones are constantly degrading and rebuilding) could also be a cause of low alk phos, though once again, would not affect a patient's management to my knowledge.
3. There are many anemias beyond iron deficiency. You need more than just the Hgb level to sort that out. MCV and RDW from your CBC would be helpful, along with the iron level, TIBC, ferritin and %sat. Depending on those tests you can go down various paths of additional testing (or stop there if you think you have a culprit).

Title: Constant feeling of needing to urinate + tingling/stimulation sensation on penis. I cannot sleep please help
Body:
Age 27

Sex Male

Height 5'7

Weight 195

Race Caucasian 

Duration of complaint 3 years

Location genitals

Any existing relevant medical issues none

Current medications none

This has been going on for three years now. I'm writing this at 9am after trying to fall asleep for the last 5 hours.

Very suddenly about 3 years ago, literally overnight, I developed a constant feeling of needing to urinate, mixed with either right side testicular pain or a tickling/tingling/stimulation feeling localized on the glans of my penis. I'm also as a result having to get up every hour or so to pee. It's just bad enough that it makes falling asleep impossible, and I never get used to it. If I can manage to fall asleep I stay asleep fine, but that usually doesn't happen. I've been to several urologists about this who were all entirely stumped. Prostate is fine, nothing unusual about the bladder or testicles under ultrasound, every antibiotic under the sun did nothing, bladder suppressant meds did nothing. They have zero idea what's wrong. 

The only thing that worked even slightly was a pelvic floor physical therapist, but only for about a day following sessions, and the at home care (stretches, massage) do nothing. Cutting out caffeine entirely does nothing. Drinking only water does nothing. Cutting out carbs does nothing. Cutting out meat does nothing. I have not been able to find a single correlation with anything I eat or do that makes it better or worse. I simply am spending 4+ hours a day attempting to sleep, and often just not sleeping at all. I am permanently sleep deprived and genuinely cannot function on a day to day basis. I would legitimately cut my own penis off if it meant I could sleep. I will try literally anything to get some relief. If anyone has any ideas, no matter how rare or niche, please let me know. I'm absolutely at the end of my rope here. This is hell and I wouldn't wish it on anyone.
Response:
Could be pudendal neuralgia/neuropathy. Might be worth it to get physical therapy from someone who specializes in this and lose some weight (due to nerve entrapment at the hip). 

Going to a pain specialist, particularly one who specializes in nerve blocks, would be a reasonable next step. 

Finally, since its been so long, there’s a high chance of central sensitization meaning that the original thing that caused the pain is no longer there but your brain is wired to perceive that it’s there since pain pathways are complex (requires both presence + perception at first but then perception can remain even in the a sense of presence).

2nd gi opinion was crohn's disease or indeterminate inflammatory bowel disease.

Both refused to let me see infectious disease specialist or test me for infections even though partner and I are having same symptoms.

Partner saw ENT because of pain in throat, ent find inflammation with no follow up.

May 2020
GP #1 orders blood work, tells me I'm crazy and that I  don't have IBD or infection.
Sends me to see his "friend" who is an infectious disease specialist.

I see infectious disease specialist a week later. He tells me there is no infection that would cause chronic inflammation.

He says it's a coincidence me and partner are sharing symptoms. 

June 2020:

I go to the ER because I'm desperate and want answers. I have stool studies sent.

I have results in album. 

July 2020:
Symptoms  get worse.

I start seeing another GP #2 to get more opinions. She orders more stool studies.

Fecal Leukocytes are positive.

Partner gets more testing and tells me he is positive for CMV infection.

I notify new GP and got tested yesterday.

I woke up this morning with my positive result and what looks like ACTIVE CMV.

Please help me, what could be causing this?

Is this a secondary infection that is activating our CMV?

What tests and infections should I be asking for and who should I see at this point?

We both we from being healthy to this within the past year.

Response:
Did you have any treatment for ulcerative colitis/IBD yet? That would be the logical first step in my opinion. 
CMV infections don't usually cause many symptoms but it certainly could be contributing in your case. You should follow up with your GP regarding the CMV serology. It may be worth repeating your HIV test.
Lastly, it's important to bear in mind that just because your partner has similar symptoms to you it doesn't mean you both necessarily have the same cause of your symptoms. 
My advice would be to stick with one GP and one or two specialists for a while and try any treatment or investigation pathways they suggest. Your case sounds quite complex and it may take some time to get you feeling better.

Title: Husband Just Told Me About "Masses" In His Lungs??!
Body:
Hello. My husband is a 37 year old uninsured male who went to the ER today for a fever that has been pretty high for about a week. There, they administered a flu test (negative) and took x-rays and determined that he has an antibiotic-resistant form of pneumonia in his right lung and a bacterial infection. 

Oh, and they mentioned some masses they observed in the lung with pneumonia. They gave him a prescription for an albuterol inhaler and some antibiotics and sent him home.

Are the masses something that we should be concerned about, because I'm kind of freaking out. Why were they so non-chalant about this??

Also, how did they determine its antibiotic-resistant pneumonia just from an x-ray and why did they prescribe antibiotics for it, if that is what it is?

ETA: He was incorrect in telling me its antibiotic-resistant pneumonia. It is antibiotic-resistant bacteria, according to his discharge papers. There is no mention of the masses in his paperwork.
Response:
Can’t diagnose an antibiotic-resistant anything (be it pneumonia, UTI, whatever) without a culture.

Pneumonia can appear “mass-like” on chest imaging. More of a CT scan descriptor than a chest x-ray descriptor but wouldn’t put it past someone to have mentioned something along those lines. He should get another chest x-ray in about 6 weeks to make sure everything has cleared up.

Title: Mom (58F) died of a aneurysm rupture in front of me yesterday, I have questions
Body:
First of all sorry if this is not the right subreddit, I don't know where to ask this.

1. Just before it arrived she said that she did not feel so good and had a huge headache, she laid down and instantly started snoring, with her eyes wide open, why does this happen ?
2. he was not responsive to anything, the person on the phone ask me to pinch her really had and she had no reaction. But she was still breathing, it was a struggle and but it seemed easier for her to breathe when I was holding her in a sitting position. How was she still able to breathe if her brain was mostly already dead ?Even after paramedics showed up, at some point they made her breathe manually (I assume she stopped), but then she started breathing again on her own, heavily but kinda normally. (the doctor even pointed it out with a kinda optimistic tone)
3. Why did she vomit ?
4. At some point the doctor was trying to force some kind of angled metal tube in her mouth / throat, it was rather large. He struggled quite a lot to put it and remove it. It did not seem like a breathing device, I assume maybe it was some kind of optical device ? So that he could see if there was a blocage of something ? Any thoughts ?
5. When did they guess it was a aneurysm rupture ? I don't know what happened in the ambulance and when she was admitted, they did a scan and it confirmed the huge bleeding, but I guess they were already pretty sure before that ?
6. She technically died the morning after, because she was still showing very small signs of brain activity, but she did not have her hooked up to a brain scan the whole time, did they ? So I guess we don't really know when the brain death happens ?Also, for me I feel like I saw her die in front of me then saw her die again the next morning, at the ER doctor said that she was in a profound coma and she would die soon, but she was not technically dead since they were some signs of brain activity still. I don't know this confuses me.
7. Also the most important question : is there any way to roughly know when she lost consciousness ? I mean, she became instantly limp and unresponsive when it happened, but people in locked in syndrome are limp and unresponsive, and they are conscious... So is there any way to know if she was conscious while I was holding her ?

​

Also why are those questions bothering me so much despite the fact that I know it does not change anything. I am a pretty curious person usually, maybe that's why.
Response:
I'm very sorry for your loss.
From the way you describe it she probably lost consciousness the moment she was on the bed and no more responsive. She was comatose because of the bleeding. Breathing still works because that is regulated from the brainstem, which is deep down in the brain. 
The paramedics probably presumed a intracranial bleeding because of the events. Headache and suddenly coma is very typical. 
The device the doctor put into her throat could be a laryngoscope, a device used to introduce a breathing tube into patients. 
The vomiting is caused by the pressure build up in the head.

Title: Help understanding my father's death
Body:
57yo male

My dad became sick about a week ago, assured us all it was just his stomach bothering him and despite being asked multiple times, he wouldn't go to a doctor. He missed work Tuesday, pushed himself to go in for approx. two hours each day Wednesday and Thursday morning and spent most of the rest of the time in bed. 

Thursday evening he was home, ate lightly, was alert and having conversations with my mom and I and claimed to be feeling better (pretty sure he was lying). Late that evening I came in from outside to see him standing over the kitchen sink coughing up blood. My mom and I tell him at this point that he has no say in the matter, he's going to the emergency room - he tells me no and not to worry about it - I go to start the car while my mom grabbed his shoes for him and attempted to phone my sister, and in less than a minute I hear my mother scream that he's on the ground. 

I get inside and he's apparently collapsed off the kitchen chair and slid to the ground, blood coming from his mouth and nose, unresponsive. My mother and I alternated doing CPR for about 20 minutes while waiting on emergency services. We're both pretty sure we saw him attempt to take a breath at least twice while doing CPR but other than that, unresponsive, no movement.

Paramedics worked on him for some time. At some point we were informed that there was a change in his heart rhythm(? I think that's how they worded it), that it wasn't beating but "quivering like it's trying to". At that point he was transported to the emergency room where they managed to briefly get a pulse back but lost it. At this point he'd been down for about an hour and a half and we were told that he was brain dead and resuscitation efforts were stopped. His heart stopped pretty quickly afterwards and he was gone.

I believe the doctor said it was a rupture of a vein in the esophagus. 

My dad was a heavy drinker and smoker (this is some dumb anonymous post on reddit so I guess it doesn't matter, but I feel like after saying that I also have to say that with his faults, he was a damn good man who loved his family more than anything and worked hard to care for us all). He was always the guy who would never go to a doctor - the last time he had a physical was when he left the Navy in the mid 80s. He always worried about his family but couldn't be convinced to take care of himself so it's difficult to pinpoint exactly all what was going on with him. 

The only definite diagnosis I know of is COPD, when he finally broke down and went to the ER a few years ago struggling to breathe. And that he had noticeably been losing weight. Other than that he was never one to complain, never one to open up, so no one really knows how he was feeling. 

It all feels so sudden. I'm just seeking more information so I can try to understand. I understand no one can give definite answers or diagnosis, but... Any thoughts are appreciated.

Googling tells me this is something that happens to heavy drinkers/people in late stages of liver disease. Is that right? How and why does this happen? My dad was really suffering and in pain in his last days, wasn't he? Am I right in feeling there was likely not much that could've been done at this stage even if we'd managed to get him to go to the doctor? (Except possibly pain management?) Did he choke on his own blood there on the kitchen floor, was it shock, cardiac arrest...? It happened so quick. Once that vein ruptured and he collapsed was he unconscious, no longer feeling pain? I truly hope he wasn't aware of what was going on past that point.

Thank you for reading and for any response.
Response:
>blood coming from his mouth and nose, unresponsive  
>  
>My dad was a heavy drinker and smoker

I'm so sorry to hear that. This is something I unfortunately see very, very often. My guess is that he had cirrhosis from alcohol use and developed varices (just as you have guessed). When you have liver disease, the liver scars down and along with neurohormonal changes, blood has trouble passing through the liver which leads to increased back pressure. The back pressure builds up and extends all the way to the esophagus where small vessels start enlarging to massive sizes. When it gets too large, these vessels (called varices) can burst leading to massive hemorrhage. Some people can bleed out a few liters of blood within an hour or less and variceal bleeding has an extremely high short- and long-term mortality risk without treatment (about 50%) due to aspiration, severe blood less and unconsciousness, or liver failure from not enough blood supply. Once he was unconscious, he did not feel anything. It was probably very quick after he lost enough blood.

The only treatment would've been to get him to the emergency room ASAP when he first started vomiting blood but even then the risk of death is very high. However, given all of that happened in such a short time, I'm not sure if he would've made it regardless.  By the time he collapsed, he was probably too sick to have survived the episode. A variceal bleed is one of about 4 or 5 GI "emergencies" where I would come in overnight to scope.

I wish your family the best. I hope this provides some closure.

Title: Will my Dad survive with a sodium level of 104 and low potassium?
Body:
56, male, 5'10, 175lbs, caucasian. Location: East Coast, USA / entire body. High blood pressure and colon polyps are the only medical conditions he has. He takes high blood pressure medication & that's it. 

​

Heart and brain are okay but his potassium was extremely low and his sodium even worse. The nurse said she's been doing this since the 90's and she's never seen a non-comatose patient with as low sodium as he has, nor did the entire ICU with shift change. They dripped a bag of saline into him and told him he needed to be admitted overnight. He refused for a good 15-20 minutes, literally yelling to leave until my family and I convinced him to stay. It took that and the doctor to tell him if he left this hospital, he would die due to a seizure and that it was basically a death sentence. If not death, brain death. 

Anyways, they admitted him, he had a potassium drip (+2 large potassium pills) and a magnesium drip. He took 3x melatonin pills to get some sleep because he couldn't sleep there on his own and was extremely tired. Lots of blood drawn. 

Is my Dad going to be okay? Genuinely? I need advice. He's my last parent alive. Thank you.
Response: The nurse wasn't exaggerating, and that definitely gives the lowest sodium I've ever seen serious competition. That's a crazy low  number. It's possible to recover if it's corrected slowly, but there's the important question of why it went so low. That's probably the most pressing issue after fixing the immediate problems.

Title: Bug in Ear aftermath, female 23

Response:
With what information you have given, I would have to guess that you may have Fibromyalgia (take this with a bit of salt as I don't have your labs nor a physical exam to go with it)

But it seems like you have generalized pain constantly, headaches, sometimes depression can be associated with it.

Most symptoms of fibromyalgia are non-specific so a doctor would have to rule out other things before labelling you with this diagnosis (thyroid issues, rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatic etc).

General things like exercise routine and proper sleep hygiene (you can google this) can help. But otherwise you would probably need a proper work up and then possibly medications.

Hope that helps

Title: I might have had a heart attack last night (i need some advice i am depressed cos my parents aren't listening to me)
Body:
I am 17(male)

I have no family history of anything

I am on medication right now(propranolol hydrochloride LA 40mg one in the morning and half at night) and magnesium tablets due to my higher heart rates(120bpm  at rest) which just started happening during these 6 months btw
