Yesterday i kept getting these strange sensations on my upper chest which led me not being able to breathe all day.At night i was just eating instant noodles where i suddenly got sweaty, nauseated,sick,clammy hands.i couldn't breathe properly while this was happening i told my mum i didn't feel right and i wanted to go to ER,but cos of my previous er trip and all the tests costing alot of money and all of em coming back normal.My mum told me that i am on medication (i mentioned)and started scolding me to stop being scared like a baby.The thing she doesn't realise that i actually thought i was dying.I went to my bed at this point the symptoms started fading its been atleast 15 mins.i am sleeping upside down and while this my right hand index and middle finger started to feel weird(I can't describe it just didn't feel right) after a few secs to a min.This mild pain started travelling slowly to my elbow few mins later it reached my shoulder and even later my back of the right shoulder (it was travelling but it kept changing its spots it didn't hurt all hand-elbow-shoulder-back at the same time)
The upper chest sensation is still there.Whenever i take a deep breath from my mouth (not my nose) i get mild pain in my upper chest.
I would like to mention that i had 100.4F fever 3 days ago and from last few days i have coughed and sneezed alot.Even while typing this my chest feels weirdly uncomfortable like an upside down U(from my upper chest to left and right breast but nothing in the center although i get dull pains in the center sometimes)


I have previously had alot of symptoms which led to ER once few months ago,had all tests coming back normal.I am 17 and healthy never had an issue in my life.These are symptoms i have had for months now which led up to this:


Chest pains(dull or sharp comes and goes within a second or two)

Both arms hurt from the shoulders down my arms to hands(mostly during evening)

Back pain(not always)

Higher HR(just going upstairs/masturbating/exercising raises my HR to 130-140 or even 160 max)(its solved now due to propranolol)

Sudden nausea(so a minute ago i will be fine but out of nowhere i will start getting nauseous i will just feel really ill)

Panic(something like nausea really freaks me out)

Chest pressure (i get these sometimes they are not in the center but below my both breasts like right below them not in the center)

Chest tightness (just happens before i go somewhere probably anxiety?)

Sweating (out of nowhere)

Crawling sensation in jaw(sometimes not always usually after i rub it with my hand then i feel something there the more i think the longer it stays)(my chin hurts sometimes aswell)

This weird sensation, I can't really explain but its some sort of grunting you get when you are really gassy but i get these on my left chest and on my back they happen in my stomach aswell.

Another weird sensation,it feels like spasms in sync with my heartbeats they increase pressure in one specific sport on left center chest and my heart feels like its not beating properly (its not fast either its not any palpitation but it does happen in sync with my heartbeats ik weird)

For days I won't get any pvcs,but whenever i get them they happen a skip a normal beat they happen again.And this happens a lot but only on that day.

Fatigue(gets triggered by anxiety)

Shortness of breath (not always usually due to anxiety)

A random punch or a kick sensation in the sensation in the chest(its not painful or hard it just happens makes me stop but its not scary i just wanted to mention it)


Tests:i had all of em i can have at this age(17) and they all came back normal.except angiography or any a ct scans as echo,ecgs,stress tests, blood tests they came back normal.

Angina attacks,Heart Attack,PE,Asthma?what is this?Even though if i am dying my parents will end up ignoring me thinking i am fine this is how my life has become.
Response:
Without any blood info, this sounds a lot like anxiety to me. You are also very young, and unless there is some rare genetic disorder or severe family history of heart attacks, you are statistically incredibly unlikely to have a heart attack. The fact that you’ve been experiencing this over many months now makes it even less likely to be an acute heart attack. 

That being said, if you think you have a heart attack, visit the ER and get tests done. This is fairly straight forward with bloods and EKG. If your heart enzymes and EKG are normal, this is most likely anxiety, with or without panic disorder. 

My money is on anxiety, and I highly recommend seeing a counselor. It’s worth it, and there is absolutely no shame in it. Taking care of yourself always takes highest priority! Good luck and get well soon.

Title: I am living out my worst nightmare. I am having serious neurological sequalae and cannot get any help because of my psychiatric history.
Body:
21 y/o male, 145 lbs / 5'11", Dx of schizoaffective d/o bipolar type w/ catatonia, for which I have been hospitalized several times. I was maintained on various antipsychotics from age 14 to 20. I received ultra-brief pulse right unilateral electroconvulsive therapy 17 times in 2016. Recovered amphetamine and opioid addict, only current medication is a low dose of buprenorphine. (I have been completely abstinent for over a year.)

Growing up on antipsychotics and being subtly socialized into a mental patient did me far more harm than good. My initial episode was as I was going into high school and was in the wake of a CPS investigation and my father's imprisonment. Yet only one doctor ever had the great idea to say, hmm, maybe this is all trauma-based in nature. Many of these hospitalizations were due to my alcoholic mother (who I am now completely dependent on) bold-faced lying to 911, and with a diagnosis like mine, I'm not expected to be able to accurately self-report. As a result, my very long medical record is almost completely filled with information that is simply false, dishonest, or miscollected. I just find it ironic that the professionals in these situations looks toward everybody *but* the actual subject of the flow of information. The ER is a very fast paced environment, and I don't blame the medical and psych workers necessarily, but it is truly shocking to me reading it, how much is just wrong or distorted. I have been treated worse than an animal or child in many of my encounters and frankly have zero inherent trust in the medical system.

This is a big part of my current issue.

For context, I was seeing a brilliant psychiatrist at an Early Psychosis Clinic who I worked with to taper safely off of all neuroleptics and an Adolescent Medicine Clinic for Primary Care at University of California, San Francisco, Mount Zion Campus to fill my Suboxone prescription. (I am not really concerned about DOX'ing myself or anybody else at this point.) I can't even "see" a Primary Care physician because this clinic is constantly cycling Docs. This leads to me trying to explain my complex concerns here with someone I just fucking met, which effectively bars any working relationship most people should be able to expect from a PCP. They consistently treated me like I was always on the verge of substance relapse despite never having a positive UA and having been on Subs and completely abstinent long before even working with them. I could not elicit any sort of actual response except scripted condescending clinical jargon. I had wanted to taper off of Suboxone because of my concerns about elevated prolactin (not caused by antipsychotics, since I haven't been on them for a long time) and insipid urine, which led to me being concerned about a central diabetes insipidus or vasopressin-related hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal issue, especially since the antipsychotic I was on last, Vraylar / cariprazine, has been reported in the nonclinical toxicology section of the FDA Drug Label to induce adrenal hypertrophy. I know that's totally tangential, but this will make sense when I describe the timeline here.

- November of 2020, I finally come off of antipsychotics, after having initiated a very lengthy taper back in 2019. (This is not "non-compliance": I was lucky enough to have a reasonable psychiatrist who shared my goal and was willing and able to support me through this.)

- December 2020, I begin to lactate. I had taken these meds for so long, and *never* did I experience high prolactin induced by neuroleptics before. Additionally, the lactation is only in one nipple. It has only gotten worse, despite the absence of antipsychotic exposure.

- [ In this time, I get a lot of my life in order and sign a book contract, join a Catholic monastic order with the aim of becoming a monk, start school, join a psychoanalytic community as a scholar in formation in order to one day become a Lacanian psychoanalyst, then get accepted to transfer to a university in Indiana with a scholarship. At this point in time, I have receded from all functional occupational activities and none of what I had previously expected of myself so nonchalantly even seems possible anymore. I mention this to state that despite the history on paper, I have always been very high functioning with a real level of achievement. Now, because of this steep plummet to disability, people honest to God think I'm intellectually disabled, when my WISC IQ was professionally tested at 143. And this is a problem because if I try to seek help, I am dealing with someone I've just met, looking at the slanderous paper trail and the pathetic, profoundly disabled man in front of them. I don't really have anyone to advocate for me, as my family will not. I have shirked away all friends and personal relationships because it is genuinely painful to string together a coherent sentence. I can't even imagine going in for a job interview at this point when I become disoriented at the grocery store check-out line. ]

- March 2021, I begin to notice a strange gait altering the way I walk. I have various non-specific physical symptoms like headache, nausea, aches, and diarrhea (despite being on Suboxone). Curiously, I developed a constant pain in my wrists that can be severe and has not relented.

- April, I start to have difficulty completing my sentences and finding the right words. (As a child, I had a stutter and clutter.) This is the primary complaint that has led to the state I'm in now, but it has gotten so, so much worse. I effectively cannot communicate verbally at the level needed to functionally survive. So, after Easter, I leave the monastery and return to my mom's house to figure things out. Then, I drop my classes, as it only gets worse.

May, I get an upper respiratory tract that was pretty bad, cough, congestion, sinus issues, et c. but what was unusual is that it lasted around 60 days. At this point everything goes to fucking shit. I basically lose my mind. My sleep becomes incredibly dysregulated, and my hair starts falling out. I instinctively grasp in a fist-like shape whenever I reach out my arm. I felt totally out of it and was hallucinating a lot. My verbal / active language abilities continue to significantly deteriorate. This is heartbreaking to me on a different level because I used to be a polyglot. I spoke four languages, and when I was 15 I wrote the only existant textbook on an indigenous Mexican language which was then published by the Universidad de Guadalajara en Jalisco. If I told someone this now, they would laugh in my face.

This continues throughout June. It is important to note that I had been trying to get a referral to a neurologist or neuroendocrinologist from the Ad. Med. PCP people since April, yet they totally ignored my concerns, and told me to talk to my psychiatrist. So, my psychiatrist just writes "Within Normal Limits" for everything, and I am stuck trying to convince Resident #24 to let me see a neurologist and that this is, in fact, *not* my baseline, and that this is seriously impairing every part of my life.

I try to seek help when twitching, tremors, and the gait change start to impair my ability to do a lot of basic shit. (Subclinical tardive syndromes or withdrawal EPS could be a factor here, I suppose.) What pushes me over the edge is when I submit my urine sample, and it comes back extremely dilute for the third time in a row. I am implicitly accused of diluting my urine or giving fake piss by the PCP team, when in fact, I had not altered anything about my drinking patterns and would like the doctors to do their fucking job of holding a reasonable curiosity about the state my health instead of just making massive assumptions.

- I go into the ER in early July, and surprise, surprise, am put on a 5150 for grave disability. The experience was torturous for reasons you could imagine. The fact that I cannot communicate well verbally, and yet, need to argue for why *I at least deserve a diagnosis of exclusion to be considered.* Everybody does, except many people don't have the fund of intellectual resources to be able to argue for themselves. Eventually, I was able to leave AMA by arguing my case in front of a judge. During the entire time, I was refused access to a hospitalist or a neurologist. I was robbed of cash. The only test done was simple blood work in the ER. But once in the psych ward, they don't even do a urinalysis. Nor do they test my prolactin, despite the fucking NP in charge of my case humiliating me by making me show her me fucking squeezing milk out of my right nipple in front of her own eyes, only to write in my 5150 about my "paranoid delusion of underlying neurological or endocrine issues." She then completely admits to me that I probably had *encephalitis*, "but it's subacute now, and it would be too cumbersome and expensive with the insurance to test for." These were her words, verbatim.

- Fucking give me a break. So, I go try to get an appointment with the PCP to follow up. They just document the ridiculous three antipsychotic medication regimen the hospital NP sent me out with, even though my psychiatrist knows I wouldn't be taking that at all. Yet, that's what's shown currently because not a word I say to these physicians can be believed. In any sort of emergency situation where I *have* to go to the ER or die, I would basically be fucked for good because of the absolute slander that is my "records." (My psychiatrist had offered to work with me to correct it.)

- I have been begging for an MRI and an immunoglobin panel, but apparently I don't deserve a diagnosis of exclusion because of such an established track record. Bullshit. No one ever investigated anything, and ultimately, these physicians are simply making an assumption without evidence. I could totally deal with it if this all turned out to be "just psychiatric." It's not going to hurt my feelings to be called crazy or told I'm just disorganized in thought / speech. But everyone, including myself, is just assuming! No one has felt the need to even just verify what I've been saying by way of prolactin test and UA. Without any basic physical evaluation and testing, it's all just conjecture and guessing.

- I decide it would be completely counterproductive to engage with these physicians anymore. I request to discharge from the clinic. I started getting my buprenorphine from an online clinic, and I plan to call my insurance to switch Primary Care Providers. Yet, they completely ignored my message about this and went ahead and charged me for some appointments I made it clear I would not be going to, anyway.

- All of these symptoms have just gotten worse, although the infection completely resolved. While in the hospital, my hips broke out with purple, paint-like (as in, non-raised, painless) spots of bruising, like flecks of color. Not sure what that was about. At this point, I have lost a lot of complex motor ability and basically speak to no one because, well, i can't. When I open my mouth, I can't say what I should. I have no idea what has happened. But people meeting me for the first time today just think I'm "like this", and it feels like a cruel nightmare that I cannot explain that *something happened*, and I have no idea what. I am so, so far from any sort of baseline ability, it's insane. I've also, weirdly, lost a lot of basic propioceptive sensation. I have given up most hopes that were completely within my reach not 8 months ago. Everything just keeps getting worse, and I don't even have an explanation to tell people as to why I'm so fucking sick and stupid now.

In short, I'm so fucking sick of reading more science than my own doctors.

Do you have any suggestions, and what should I do to in order to see an actual, real-life neurologist sooner than later? Can I find one covered by my insurance without a referral? Or, if I wanted to just find a private practice neurologist myself, would I have to just pay out of pocket? Thank you for reading; I know some of this is confusing, and there is a lot of frustration in my voice.
Response: Does your insurance require you to get referred to a neurologist? Even if it does, you can just call around and get an appointment with one and pay cash. Ideally you’d want a neurologist and a psychiatrist with a good working relationship with you and each other.

Title: Do ICU doctors have the right to remove feeding tube and stopping care on a patient?
Body:
Hi all! My brother (40 years old) was in the ICU for 2.5 weeks last month, and about 1.5 weeks in, the ICU doctors decided to remove the feeding tube and stop care without consulting the family. They said his situation was futile and there was no hope for care, even though we wanted them to continue care (he eventually passed away because he didn't have any food or medicine).

My question is...do ICU doctors have the right to remove feeding tube and stopping care on a patient? They claimed they had that right because more than one doctor agreed on it. However, we never met with ANYONE from the hospital to discuss this at all. I am in the state of Michigan if this helps any (and he was not brain dead). Appreciate any guidance on this.
Response:
Well, it depends. State laws differ and I saw that you pointed out that you were in Michigan. According to some research, the State of Michigan determines that a patient is dead if one of the two apply: "\[i\]rreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions" *or* "\[i\]rreversible cessation of all functions of the entire brain, including the brain stem."

Since claim that your brother was not brain dead, then he must have had cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions.

I am not an attorney, but the doctors should have at least consulted with the family before making the decision. Is it illegal that they didn't? Not really to be honest. Was it inappropriate? Yes, it was.

I also did research and do believe that physicians in Michigan can legally remove a patient off of life support, but many variables come into play before this determination can be made without consent. I would suspect that these doctors knew their laws and what they were doing; however, it is your right to contact an attorney regarding this matter.

Title: (TW) Do I *need* to be medically treated for this overdose? If so, don't want to be admitted to psych
Body:
I'm a 23y/o female, 5'5, about 115lbs. About 2 1/2 days (60 hrs) ago, I took 12,500mg of acetaminophen at once with intent of wanting to end my life. 

 Currently, I'm eating few small meals each day (my nausea prevents me from wanting to eat and I'm getting full extremely quickly). A headache and weakness/fatigue have been/are preventing me from doing anything mildly physical -  I went home sick from work the day after the overdose, and today I was able to do some housework for about half an hour, but needed to lie down immediately afterwards. I'm not jaundiced at all, and I don't have any liver pain, though I have stabbing pains periodically behind my left ribcage (pancreas/spleen area). 

Obviously I'm aware that I should visit the ER. All the symptoms I've listed above are making me extremely uncomfortable, to the point where I want to be unconscious (I know that's not how acetaminophen overdoses work) or I want to be treated (I don't even think NAC would be able to be administered at this point). However, I will avoid at all costs being admitted for inpatient psych treatment. Having been admitted a few times before, I know it has not ever worked for me; only made me feel reliant and vulnerable  (I'm a very independent person and get upset when I cannot make my own decisions/take care of myself when I am able). 

With an overdose of this degree, is it at all possible I will recover any time soon with at least diminished symptoms? If not (and this is the only way I will go to the hospital), is there a way to receive medical treatment without being admitted for psych treatment afterwards? I believe the serum acetaminophen will be virtually undetectable at this point, so unexplained liver damage \*might\* be believable. But I've been admitted/treated for an acetaminophen overdose before, so I imagine it would be suspected. I know if it's found out that I have tylenol poisoning I'd be put on psych hold, which I'd be fine with - I just don't want inpatient psych treatment following medical treatment.
Response:
You need to go to the ER now. Acetaminophen overdose causes delayed hepatic failure, and some of your symptoms are indicative of impending failure. I understand you do not want to be admitted for psych, but you really need to have your liver looked at. If the liver failure doesn't kill you, it may leave you with long-term problems if not treated. The hope would be to improve your mental state, and you do not want to live the rest of your life with a non-functional liver from this one mistake.

Furthermore, you may not be admitted to an in-patient psychiatric facility but may have a psychiatrist see you. Ultimately it would be up to the psychiatrist to admit you to an inpatient hospital setting, not the primary doctor that is taking care of the liver. I wish you the best.

Title: I am 84 y/o and was Healthy. Please assist a retired physician.
Body:
Hi I am an 84 year old female. The last two years my husband has been in and out of hospitals. Prior to was very healthy no problems whatsoever. In September 2019 I started feeling very tired, lethargic, made it difficult to walk. Pain started to spread to bones, muscles.... doctor dx (diagnoses) with fibermyalgia and prescribed prednisone 40mg.  The last time my husband was in the hospital being December 2019 I especially felt it difficult to navigate the day. To walk. To breathe. Pain all over. 

My arthritis results came back negative January 2020. 

Upon visiting a physician he noticed that my oxygen is very very low. It was under 80. As a result the emergency the spirometer and had CT scan with contrast of my entire chest where they discovered fibrosis? In the lower lobes. Since then I have been instructed to increase my o2 intake full time. I am not feeling better - without oxygen. 2-5 minutes of breathing w/out and then pressure in chest transpires. 

Now let’s discuss COVID - since a good portion of my degradation in lung capacity has decreased - I tested negative for COVID and for antibodies. I am still under quarantine. 

I am very uneasy as my primary, and specialist, cannot seem to confidently describe my diagnosis. I am here, posting, desperately seeking other individuals and professionals which may have experience and or questions. I am happy to use this as a discussion forum and provide any and all information absolutely necessary to determine or at least try my diagnosis. 

Personally - I am at a loss. My husband - a physician - and myself working at the practice feel even more powerless to mother nature’s wrath. 

I remain positive - and everyone - I have accepted the responses received may be negative. My overall goal is to lead as long of a manageable life as possible and visit the casino with my Grandson!

I have been taking metformin as I was diagnosis with type II diabetes. Other include inderal. Metformin. Zoloft. Took ambien at night. And Lorzatan.
Response:
Sounds like you need a pulmonologist. The CT showed fibrosis. This is a very all-encompassing finding if you will that can represent a whole host of underlying causes. Further advanced imaging, biopsy, bronchoscopy, and many blood tests can get you closer to an answer, but these are things for your pulmonologist to go over with you.

I would be remiss to say that at 84 it's very important to consider how invasive you want to get in terms of further studies. Obviously it's important to improve your quality of life, but the risk/benefit calculus is a very personal one, and though I don't know you, I'm just saying it's essential to consider.

Title: Severe postpartum incontinence... One year and it's still going strong
Body:
I am a 44 y/o F, I had my first and only baby 16 months ago. She was delivered via c section after about four hours of pushing (her head was in the birth canal the entire time), due to the fact that she was just not in the correct position to deliver. The immediate postpartum recovery was uneventful. Any third trimester leaking I had been dealing with diminished, and I went back to a very normal bathroom routine. 

At 4 months postpartum, something literally just went wrong. One day while I was preparing lunch, I felt the usual/typical feeling that I'd need to use the bathroom soon. That feeling, however, was accompanied by an urgency and the INSTANT feeling like a dam bursting: I just literally urinated everywhere and I had ZERO control over holding it in. Alarmed, I cleaned up/showered/changed and assumed this was a one time thing. I was wrong. From that afternoon on, this is exactly what happens when I have to use the bathroom. And it is a time-consuming, never-ending cycle: The feeling comes on to use the bathroom, immediately followed by a fierce feeling of urgency and my bladder cannot hold it. It is FULL flow, soaking through overnight Poise pads, underwear, and pants, and causing me to have to change clothes and clean up in the shower after EVERY incident. These accidents are happening every 2-3 hours, and every clean up takes a minimum of 15-20 minutes each time. 

it interferes so horribly with my ability to be the mother that my baby deserves. My husband has to work from home in order to take over with her every single time I have an accident that I have to go and clean up again and again. I can't leave the house for very long or go far, because if I have an accident out, how on earth am I going to deal with it?! It is taking such a huge toll on me. I visited a new obgyn for an exam last summer when we moved to a new town, one month after this all started, and was told it would just "go away on its own" and "give it about a year to work itself out." She said it was too soon to refer me to a urologist, and my pelvic floor muscles just needed to strengthen back up. 

I tried everything I was instructed to try... Vaginal weights, keagle exercises, using the bathroom normally every 30 minutes, absolutely no improvement. I can't shake the feeling that this problem isn't going to just go away on its own or be solved with muscle exercises. Something really messed up within my bladder. This is not a situation where I "leak" if I sneeze or laugh. I would be so lucky if that were the problem.. But this problem is a fierce urgency to go, followed by immediate full-flow urination. I literally cannot hold it in. Does this sound like urge incontenince? Or something more complicated? Do I even have any options for relief? Is there ANY light at the end of the tunnel???
Response:
You're having uninhibited detrusor contractions. The bladder muscle is contracting and you can't stop it. 

Send me a PM with your location and I'll recommend a specialist for you to see. 

FWIW, this is my specialty.

Title: Dad's Passing - Age 44, Hit His Head, BAC .44
Body:
I'm just hoping a doctor can help give me insight in my father's last moments.

In February my father was discovered, having passed away a few days later. It was a bit of a gory scene, as he hit his head and there was a lot of blood everywhere. From what I've been told it looks like he was crawling towards the bathroom in his final moments.

I hadn't seen my father much because of the pandemic and even more so because he was an alcoholic - I saw him briefly around Christmas as he dropped off presents and he was drunk and his mouth was purple and it was very unsettling. Unfortunately that was the last time I saw him. 

The toxicology report finally came in and I was told his official cause of death is Acute Ethanol Intoxication and that his BAC was .44

I've looked it up and it seems that is an extremely dangerous and almost impossible to reach level but I do know he was drinking a lot for a long time. When he would stop drinking he would actually get seizures and was recently diagnosed with Epilepsy because of it. 

The one thing that really haunts me is wondering about his final moments. He died alone crawling through his blood and I wonder how much he suffered and how conscious he was of everything. Finding out about this high alcohol level, does this mean he, at least, didn't suffer in these final moments? Also, for him to have such a high tolerance to alcohol and to be drinking this much, even though he ended up falling and hitting his head, was it just a matter of time before his body failed? He was always so thin and looked so old even though he was just 44 when he died. 

He was a college professor, he was a smart man, he was just a sad one. 

I appreciate any responses to help me understand what happened in his final moments.
Response:
I’m so sorry for your loss.

It’s very hard to know what exactly happened, but you’re correct in thinking that with a BAC that high, he was not fully aware of what was going on and any pain or discomfort would have been dulled. He sounds like he was quite unwell, and likely was facing a number of serious health issues as a result of his alcohol use. It is very very unlikely he would have lived to an average life expectancy. You are correct that if someone is using that much alcohol, it can become “a matter of time” before something serious happens. 

Again - I’m very sorry about your Dad.

Title: Why don't they inject chemo directly into my son's tumor instead of poisoning his entire body with it?
Body:
Age 2

Sex M

Height 28"

Weight 24lbs

Race W

Duration of complaint birth

Location sacrococcygeal teretoma 

Any existing relevant medical issues no

Current medications chemo / zofran / emend / benadryl / fluids / nuepogen / bactrim
Response:
The goal of chemotherapy in solid tumor treatment is to shrink the tumor prior to surgery in order to make excision easier, and also to prevent metastasis both before and after surgery. 

Locally injected chemotherapy would not treat the entire tumor, and also would do nothing to prevent metastasis, which occurs on a microscopic level. I sometimes describe it as “cleaning up cancer dust.”

The simplest answer is because that’s what your son’s physicians have to do in order to save his life. 

Credential: I am board-certified in pediatric hematology & oncology.

Title: Constantly loud blood - my pulse is projected from my throat/mouth and other people can hear it.
Body:
18F, 170cm 48kg 

Heart rate is around 60bpm. Usually my blood pressure is low - normal. Non-smoker. 

Here's a recording -  

It is constant, consistent, and very annoying. I recorded that just by opening my mouth wide and holding my phone close. It's like I swallowed a metronome or something. No symptoms of respiratory infection. No phlegm, nose is clear, 0 cold symptoms. No hayfever. 

My mum can hear it if I put my mouth near her ear. She says it occurs at the same time as the pulse in my neck.

It happens regardless of the positioning of my mouth, neck, or tongue. It happens whether I breathe or stop breathing. If I expand my lungs to the point of discomfort, it stops whilst lungs are still in that state, but instantly resumes. If I deflate my lungs as much as possible, it also momentarily stops. Otherwise, it is constant. I don't hear any thumping, just this clicking/ticking noise. There is no sensation of thumping or pounding. 

Duration - Noticed a few days ago but may have been ongoing prior. 

Location - The sound feels like it's coming from my carotid artery at about the space between the ear and the jaw and is projected by my mouth. Geographic location is Australia, where it is currently Spring. 

Any existing relevant medical issues - Collapsed chest wall (pectus excavatum, severe) that once compressed and displaced my heart to the left, but now corrected with Nuss early this year. Two titanium bars under ribcage and sternum. I don't know where my heart is now. I had a heart ultrasound about two years ago as part of screening for Marfan syndrome (don't have it) and there wasn't anything of particular significance.
Response: With your history of pectus excavatum, I suspect you might have some connective tissue disease, and if other people can hear this pulsatile sound I am worried that you might have a vascular malformation or aneurysm. I would seek prompt evaluation by your primary care doctor, and specifically ask about this possibility. You may ultimately need a CT angiogram.

Title: I fear my dad will die from sepsis due to his diabetic foot infection
Body:
My dad \[62M\] was diagnosed with type two diabetes somewhere between late 2018 and early 2019, after going to the doctor for significant foot pain. My dad has some mental health issues, and isn't someone to go to the doctor unless he absolutely needs to, and if he does go, he only wants medicine.

Fast-forward to now, and his foot infection is so bad that he can barely walk. His foot and toes are giant, and from the knee down, his leg is blown up like a balloon. He is in denial, BAD, and keeps taking different antibiotics, but it seems to me that what he really needs is to get his foot or lower leg amputated before an infection moves into his blood stream.

He does not watch his diet, doesn't monitor his glucose, and I just found out recently that he started smoking again. He will not let any of his family members including his kids go to the doctor with him. He is single, and does not have a wife or girlfriend. He's extremely secretive about the information from his appointments and will tell us as little as possible.

It sounds like his doctor told him that she will only prescribe him another two-weeks worth of antibiotics and then that's it.

He has let this go so long and is in such denial that my siblings and I are left feeling completely hopeless. It feels like he is slowly committing suicide right in front of us. I have tried everything to get through to him; I have cried to him in person, written him letters, offered to create a meal-plan for him, we stay on top of him about his appointments, offer to take him to the hospital, etc.

Are there any resources for this type of situation? Is there someone I can call who specifically works with people who are in complete denial about their life-threatening condition? He refuses therapy or any type of mental health services. I am at a loss for what to do next. I desperately don't want to say goodbye to my dad.

Thank you in advance for your help and time.
Response:
There are lots of things available to people who struggle with diabetes. There are dieticians to help with meal planning and general guidance. Tbrrr are therapists to work on denial and barriers to sticking with treatment. There can be home services, from aides to visiting nurses, that can help with practical problems with getting or taking medications right.

All of those require a patient who wants help getting better. That sounds like the issue with your dad. He doesn’t want to take care of himself. That itself might be something that can be worked on—but he’s have to show up and do it. Otherwise you’re just waiting for a crisis, and trying to manage crisis to crisis is a bad way through healthcare.

It’s very hard to have a family member who is self-destructing but refusing to let you or anyone else intervene. Unfortunately for you, people are allowed to make bad decisions even when those decisions have terrible consequences. As long as he’s in his right mind, he can be in denial to the point of having treatable minor problems become unsolvable and fatal problems. If you physically drag him to the hospital it’s possible that under emergency circumstances he might get an amputation, but again, if he’s sound-minded and just refuses, he’s allowed to. 

You and your family have my sympathy. I hope you can get through to him, and I hope someone else has a better suggestion.

Title: Confusing situation
Body: 69 year old female, in the US. A few days ago I was on vacation in the US. I ate lunch at restaurant #1, then 6 hours later I ate dinner at restaurant #2. I had French Onion soup at restaurant #1, and it was kind of nasty looking, and it wasn't hot. I know enough about food service to know that hot food should be served hot, otherwise bacteria grows. I only ate half of the soup. About bedtime I felt a little queasy, but I thought "oh well it will pass". I go to sleep. Awhile later I wake with vomit in my mouth. I go to the bathroom and vomit. I have onions coming out of my nose. My face really hurts, for some reason. So I lay down in bed, and I can't move. I can't lift a finger. I can't speak. I am breathing fast. My husband calls 911. They come, and haul me to the ER. In the ER I can't speak, I can't move, I can't open my eyes, and I am breathing really hard. I had no diarrhea. I manage to squeeze out a few words when the nurse was asking me questions, but I couldn't say much. The staff didn't seem to realize the condition I was in. They gave me Morphine and Zoloft, even though I wasn't nauseated, and the pain was minimal, and IV fluids, then sent me back to the hotel. The nurse pushed the wheelchair to the door of the car and I managed to get in the car. My speech was slurred for almost 24 hours, my face was swollen, I could not breathe through my nose, I was exhausted. Now, 72 hours later, I still don't feel that great. I have a headache.  I can walk and talk. I can't figure out what actually happened to me. The lab work showed that I was slightly dehydrated. So, anyone have an idea of what happened? Thank you.
Response: Kind of sounds like botulism? Look up those symptoms and see what you think. Certainly could happen from a meal. Note: would be a very mild case.

Title: 50+ y/o (f) let me tattoo her face 3x before telling me …

Title: Stuck on manual breathing
Body:
Hello all,

A couple hours ago as I was trying to fall asleep, I was in the zone where I was like half awake and half asleep. Though, suddenly, I started thinking like “damn, you’re gonna forget to breathe and die” for whatever reason. So I was completely roused from my attempts to sleep and have been manually breathing ever since. 

I have tried doing some random activities across the house and on my phone to distract myself so that my subconscious will take over the breathing task but before I can fully “immerse” myself, I remember and keep manually breathing instead.

I’ve also tried falling back asleep, but the same thing happens as earlier. I would be about to fall asleep, then as I’m about to fully fall asleep, my lungs feel like I’m neglecting the breathing task and I wake myself up.

I am an 18 year old male, somewhere around the 5’10, 180 lbs mark, body fat percentage somewhere around 22% I would estimate. I am not on any medication, and this has never happened before say outside of memes that say “you will now manually breathe,” but I would forget about it seconds later.

I was thinking that this continues due to my inability to stop thinking about it, but I was wondering if there’s any physiological factors at play here as well. Thank you
Response:
If your brain stem is functioning and you don't have a congenital defect in your CO2 sensing system, you'll keep breathing. You literally will just have to get distracted enough to stop thinking about it.  

While my little patients love to forget to breathe a lot, for big people, the urge to breathe is so strong that you can't stop yourself, even if you wanted to (if you hold your breath until you are unconscious, you will start breathing the moment you aren't actively suppressing it.  

Maybe think about it that way. Your breathing is an automatic function and when you "manually" breathe, you are simply overriding that automatic function for a short period.  But if you stop concentrating on overriding your natural system, the natural system will work.

Title: 22F - took medication for ADHD for five days and I haven’t been the same since
Body:
22F - United States - Caucasian - 137 lbs - 5’5 - currently taking birth control and 50 mg Prozac for anxiety/depression, no other drug use besides occasional alcohol - no other medical conditions besides ADHD

In September my psychiatrist prescribed me 18mg Concerta. I took it for four days with no bad effects, but on the fifth day I began having symptoms like possible seizures. I was shaking uncontrollably (started with my jaw, then my head and arms) and also felt very out of it. My vision would get very blurry and I would start to feel like I was losing consciousness. My mom witnessed this and said it looked like seizures, but I’ve never had anything like that happen before so I’m not sure. 

I went to urgent care and they basically just gave me fluids and said to stop taking the medication, and that it should go away within 24 hours. The doctor also mentioned serotonin syndrome as a possibility but didn’t seem concerned. 

The effects have not stopped in the past month. I still get the shaking and have episodes where I just feel really weird and out of it, almost like I am asleep even though my eyes are open and I’m awake. I get weird feelings in my head at times, not pain but a feeling of pressure. My brain has been so slow lately, I’m forgetting passwords that I know, it takes me a long time to think of certain words. I’m not really sure where to go from here. Should I schedule an appointment with just a regular doctor? I don’t have a primary care physician right now
Response:
Clinically this does not sound like serotonin syndrome. Yes some of your symptoms may be similar but the rest of the description doesn’t match. As well, Concerta 18mg is a relatively low dose of a drug that theoretically can but very rarely would be a contributor to serotonin syndrome. 

A bit on the clinical signs in serotonin syndrome: “Mental status changes can include anxiety, restlessness, disorientation, and agitated delirium [13]. Patients may startle easily. Autonomic manifestations can include diaphoresis, tachycardia, hyperthermia, hypertension, vomiting, and diarrhea [3]. Neuromuscular hyperactivity can manifest as tremor, myoclonus, hyperreflexia, and bilateral Babinski sign. Hyperreflexia and clonus are particularly common; these findings, as well as rigidity, are more often pronounced in the lower extremities [3]. In severe cases, muscle rigidity may mask myoclonus and hyperreflexia.”

There are a number of other diagnoses that I would consider more likely:
- intolerance to Concerta. It’s possible your body is poor at metabolizing a byproduct of the drug and it built up in your system over the 5 days you took it and now you’re waiting for your body to clear the byproduct which is of course going to take longer than normal for you. 
- have you had any alcohol? I’ve seen a case where my patient went day drinking (St Patrick’s) after taking his Concerta and had a lots of those similar symptoms. Took him a couple weeks to get over it completely. 
- I’ve also had numerous patients start stimulants like Concerta for possible ADD/ADHD and, because poor concentration is a shared symptom with many conditions, the new medication brought out new symptoms of their actual underlying issue. Psychosis, bipolar, severe anxiety, and epilepsy I’ve all seen and I’m sure there are more. 

Anyway, I’d recommend reassessment by both a general physician and your psychiatrist. Best time to do so would be soon as their best bet to figure out what’s happening is assessing you while you’re showing symptoms. It’s a lot more difficult to diagnose someone based on “I think I felt this symptoms last week”. 

Best of luck!

Title: Symptoms of breast cancer, feel discriminated against And not taken seriously by doctors because of my weight
Body:
TLDR; I know doctors hate it when the patient plays google doctor. However, I feel it is important to be educated when something potentially serious is going on with you. So I have done some reading (from reputable sources and medical journals) and strongly feel I am exhibiting symptoms of breast cancer. I feel doctors have ignored this because of my weight.

Background: I am a 25 year old female and now weigh nearly 250 lbs, almost 5’9”. Doctors have told me they think I have PCOS. I have been putting on weight for some time now, doctors have Said this gain could be due to the PCOS, however over 15lbs of the 30 or so I’ve gained in the last year has been in the last two months. And I’ve been actively trying to lose weight, even taking Contrave (bupropion/naltrexone) to help with my appetite. I also have a mirena IUD for BC and take spironolactone and Slynd (progesterone only oral BC) for cystic acne. They Slynd I’ve only been taking for three months.  


Symptoms: Aside from the weight gain, I have one breast that has rapidly grown in size (it seemed to happen in the span of about four days) and is now over a cup size bigger than the other. Both breasts suddenly have increased vein prominence, some blueish discoloration (almost like bruising), I’ve had red dots appear on the skin and the skin on my upper chest suddenly feels bumpy and scaley, and both are very sore and aching. Both have leaked completely clear discharge from the nipples when lightly expressed. Under my arms and into my back are quite sore as well. I feel generally tired as well.

I went to see a midwife in OBGYN for the first available appointment And she found a lump on the larger breast. I’m scheduled for an ultrasound on the 30th. However, when I left a message to say that they had become even more sore and to inform her about the new discharge, I was called by a nurse, told the midwife spoke to some doctors, and they wanted me seen in general surgery that day (this past Thursday).

The surgeon I saw was very rushed (they must have squeezed me in) and did an improper breast exam, not even feeling where I told him the lump had been found. He told me “nothing I was experiencing was a symptom of cancer.” And I “shouldn’t lose sleep over it.” He offered to give me antibiotics but said he “wasn’t sure what he’d be treating” so I refused them. He told me if I just lost 35-45lbs a lot of my “problems would go away”. He questioned whether or not I showered everyday. He was accusatory, telling me the timeline of my breast growth “just didn’t make sense”. I told him well, yeah, that’s why it’s concerning. He told me to see an endocrinologist for my hormones and weight and suggested cosmetic surgery for both my increased unilateral breast size and my weight.

I was offended. I felt ignored. I felt confused. Why was I told to rush in just to be blown off like that? I know from researching that these can all be symptoms of breast cancer. I feel like my symptoms are all being blamed on my weight rather than thinking about how sudden and rapid the weight gain was and that it may possibly be a symptom not the problem. 

I’m hoping this is a hormone issue, maybe due to the PCOS, but am afraid it’s something worse, like breast cancer.

 I feel at a loss right now. So many questions. How do I deal with what I feel is weight discrimination in a medical setting? Are these symptoms more concerning than doctors are letting on? What hormonal issue could cause these problems, if it is that? Why have the doctors been dodging my questions about it being cancer? Has anyone else experienced anything like this?

Any help would be greatly appreciated!
Response: Lots of possibilities here. Nothing sounds suspiciously like breast cancer to me (rapid cup size changes are not typical for breast cancer, and spironolactone may be a big confounder here). But it is good you are getting an ultrasound for the lump since you are concerned. Your symptoms do sound like things an endocrinologist should look at, especially with the variety of hormone treatments you are on and that large weight gain and unusual muscle soreness

Title: I tested positive for tuberculosis, but my doctors say I don't need treatment. Are they right?
Body:
Last week, my physician called me to tell me ( 24F ; 5'6'' ; 170 lbs ) my bloodwork (EliSpot-test) came back positive for tuberculosis (I never got the BCG vaccine since my country doesn't recommend it, so a false positive isn't likely). I got a chest X-Ray which came back normal, and I'm still waiting for the results of my spit test (they're doing a PCR one and a colony one). I have no symptoms apart from a chronic cough I've had for years which has always been attributed to a hyperreactive bronchial system.

I've been told by my physician as well as by another doctor specialised on infectious diseases that this means I have LTBI (latent tuberculosis infection) and if the spit test comes back negative, treatment won't be necessary.

I live in a Western European country, but everything I've read from the CDC to WHO to the NHS says that treating LTBI is important and that, if left untreated, I might become ill and infect other people. I really don't want this to happen.

So, who is right: My doctor or the guidelines I read online?

And do I have to disclose LTBI before travelling?
Response:
A positive test (PPD) doesn't mean you have tuberculosis; it means you were exposed to the bacteria. The gold standard is a sputum test, where lab technicians will try and grow the bacteria to identify it's exact type. 

A clean x-ray is a good sign and shows no tuberculomas.

Title: Is this a good selection of procedures for a healthy 34yo male?
Body:

I'll be honest, the sedative gastric endoscopy scares me, I've never done something like that before. 

Do you think this is a good selection of procedures for a healthy 34 year old male, athletic build, non-smoking, non-drinking?
Response:
No, I don't think it is. There are a bunch of things in there that are entirely medically unnecessary unless you have symptoms warranting them. You don't need an EKG, pulmonary function tests, chest X\-ray, tumor markers, some of that bloodwork, abdominal ultrasound, endoscopy, or stool studies.

A basic physical exam with blood pressure and possibly some blood and urine analysis \+ STI testing would absolutely suffice. At your age, the most important thing is just to discuss ways to keep yourself healthy.

Title: My mother is 48 and definitely has Alzheimer's and is denying everything about it. What can I do now?
Body:
* My mom is a she.
* She is 48.
* She weighs 130, I believe. I've never asked my mom to step on a scale for me.
* She smokes.
* She likes alone in the woods of Maine.
* She has digestive issues.


About 5 years ago is when I first started to notice she was having consistent memory lapses. But they were not horrible lapses or over anything important, just consistent. I said she should see a doctor about her mind. She said she would. Every time I've asked about it since they she's said "Yup, I've made an appointment." Well, I've been waiting for her to come home and tell me how her appointment went for 5 years, and today she forgot the word for 'coat' and 'soup' and staggered down to the other end of the house to have the same conversation with me and hug me goodnight 7 times in a row.


It used to come in spells that would last maybe an hour to 3 hours where she would change from her normal self to someone who was a little mean, spoke in disjointed sentence fragments, slurred her words, forget where she was going, forget what she was currently doing, remember what she was doing, and then forget that she just remembered what she was doing, rearranging things that don't need anything done to them, drive on the wrong side of the road, go way over the speed limit without realizing it, staggering while walking as if she was drunk, dropping things like shes a clutz and all while hunched over like the The Hunchback of Notre-Dame but with her face stuck in the expression of terrified fish.



And then suddenly she'd be fine. She'd be back to her normal intelligent, astute, kind, patient, articulate and methodical self. I've tried to talk to her about this and she's always said nothing was wrong but she totally has an appointment scheduled anyway so I don't need to worry about it.



But today she was like this the whole day and it was worse than ever before. From the moment she woke up until the moment I finally got her to go to sleep around midnight she was like this. Like I said she forgot the words for 'coat' and 'soup' and got mad when I asked if she realized that forgetting nouns like that was probably bad. I needed to use her phones internet for job searching tonight so she knew she had to bring her phone to me before bed. She did that talked to me a bit, hugged me and said goodnight, walked down to the end of the hallway, and then began looking for her phone so she could text her brother. She came down to me to ask me to help her find her phone so she could text her brother before she gave it to me for the night. I explained that her phone was on the desk in front of her because she just brought it down to me. She than took it, texted her brother. Talked to me a bit, hugged me said goodnight, and then came back for the same thing seven more times in a row. Seven. Each time I asked her if she remembered just doing the same thing a moment before, she got mad and said that'd not what happened but she totally was meaning to do this.



I'm only home to witness this because I was able to afford to take a bus to visit her for the holidays. I live 70 miles away and I have no idea what to do. Neither of us have any money. If not for the thing where it comes in spells of 1 hour to at most 3 hours (except for today) this looks exactly like Alzheimer's. I have no idea what to do. All I can do is hope she's back to normal when she wakes back up. But I'm sure she'll deny everything while also maintaining that she meant to do everything she did yesterday.
Response: You need to take her to the ED when this happens. Frankly, it sounds more like drug use than Alzheimers, but it could also be B12 deficiency, severe alcoholism, strokes, seizures, a tumor, or a wide variety of serious conditions. If she is not cognizant enough to make decisions for herself, which it sound like she isn't, then you can call an ambulance for her and have her evaluated in the emergency room.

Title: Collapsing at random. Unable to move, but conscious.
Body:
20f, 5'7" 104lbs, white, diagnosed with generalized and social anxiety. Taking Wellbutrin 250mg for it and it works well. Non drinker non smoker. No history of panic disorder, seizures, or hypoglycemia.

This has been happening since I was about 15-16, and has occurred about 6 times until now. It typically happens once or twice a year, although it's becoming more frequent (last episode was yesterday, episode before that was only a month ago). 

Episodes typically consist of feeling a heaviness in my abdomen and lightheadedness. It's hard to describe, but I can feel them coming on. My body feels very cold and I start to sweat profusely. There is extremely loud ringing in the ears and tunnel vision, along with pinprick sensations (like a limb that's fallen asleep) in the hands. In severe episodes, I will collapse and appear to be unconscious, but I am fully awake and aware of my surroundings even though I can't move or speak. Episodes where I can remain standing are typically associated with nausea, sometimes to the point of vomiting.

There are no feelings of panic, racing heart, difficulty breathing, or feeling a loss of control. I've had panic attacks, and this does not feel like a panic attack at all.

These typically last for about 10-15 minutes. There is very little consistency in where and why this happens, although they only happen when standing for long periods of time. It's happened during house tours, fashion shows, school, and concerts. What's confusing to me is that I am able to stand for long periods (10+ hrs) at work, so I don't know if standing is the sole trigger for this. I think not eating has something to do with it, but I can't remember if there's a consistent pattern of not eating before these happen.

I've spoken to doctors and therapists about this, and they say they're not sure. I've been told it's just anxiety, but anxiety treatments have no effect on it and these episodes are not associated with anxiety. 

I'm very concerned because I'm going into a field that requires standing all day, and I'm afraid this may become incapacitating.

Title: White poop
Body:
Obligatory info: Caucasian female, 18, 5’8”, 99lbs, no meds or illnesses. 

Friday morning I had food poisoning that leveled me for two solid days, when on Sunday I started feeling a little better. Monday I felt much better, and it’s now early Tuesday and I feel mostly human again. However my stomach is still very temperamental and I can feel/hear it bubbling constantly. I can only eat a very little bit before I don’t feel good again, so now I’m practically dealing with hunger pains and discomfort pain constantly. I had diarrhea all weekend, per the food poisoning, but when I could have a little solid food again my stool also solidified (still having diarrhea though). 

However, since Friday I’d say this is the second or third time I’ve had almost white, half formed stool with white chunks inside it. Usually preceded by a much bigger feeling of stomach upheaval as well. Regrettably I don’t have a picture of my stool at this time lol. I’m wondering if this is a big cause for concern right now, or if it’s still related to the food poisoning working its way out? 

I hope it’s not a big deal because I’m currently in a situation with no doctor, no insurance, and no money... :/
Response:
Typically white/clay colored stool indicates a lack of bile in your GI tract. Other anti-diarrheal medications such as Pepto-Bismal can also do this. Are you having any other symptoms such as pain in your right upper abdomen (just beneath your rib cage)? 
Since you recently had food poisoning it’s possible you basically evacuated the majority of the bile in your guy, and since you’ve haven’t really been eating your gallbladder hasn’t been stimulated to release a whole lot more. So as a result you’ve got pale colored poop. If you otherwise feel ok I would recommend waiting 24-48 more hours to let your gut settle out and see if this clears up on its own. However if you develop a fever, persistent and severe abdominal pain, or notice a yellowing of the whites of your eyes then you need to get into an Emergency Room promptly. If this problem doesn’t resolve in 48 hours, but you still feel ok otherwise, then a scheduled visit to your doctor would be appropriate. Hope this helps and I hope you feel better.

Title: My partner [27/F] has some serious issues with her back passage and we don't know what to do. (Attempt 2)
Body:
I posted this 15 days ago and got no responses. I'm gonna try again because I really want some answers to this.

Apologies if my explanation of what's going on goes a little all over the place, I'm not really sure what the best way to go about explaining everything is, but I did the best I could to get things as coherant and understandable as possible while explaining as much as I can about everything that's happening.

Feel free to offer any feedback on how I can re-word this to explain things better or ask any clarification questions you may have.

And please carefully read the whole thing before you comment any suggestions or anything. Thank you.

​

About three years ago now, my partner developed a health problem.

It started out small but just kept getting worse and worse and causing other issues alongside it, and now everything's just gotten extremely bad.

​

Let's get the medical details out of the way first. We don't know my partner's current weight (though she is a bit on the chubby side), her height is about 6 foot, she doesn't smoke, doesn't drink any alcohol, doesn't take any drugs, not currently taking any medicine and has no known current medical issues (except maybe some undiagnosed anxiety issues)

​

Okay so let's start with the symptoms of my partner's health problem. They are as follows;

**Symptom 1)** Yellow or brown (Or somewhere in between) liquid (Not watery, more mucus-y) discharge (Before you say it, it's not diarrhea or constipation) from the butthole that takes more than one roll of toilet paper to wipe off before it stops. Especially after going number 2. It just never seems to stop coming after a number 2. Every time she wipes, there's discharge.

It's gotten to the point of where she doesn't bother to keep wiping until it finally decides to completely stop, but rather get it down to where it's only a little bit coming out and then move on to other things while she waits for it to eventually stop on its own.

This discharge doesn't always appear when going number 1, I think.

We are using wet wipes as a replacement for TP to clean things up but it still takes several packets a day. So it's either spend a few quid on a big packet of TP daily or spend a few quid on several packs of wet wipes daily.

Works out to more or less the same amount of money spent over the same period of time either way.

**Symptom 2)** Tiny specks of what we can only assume is fecal matter being deposited from her butthole into her buttcrack. Again, taking multiple rolls of paper to remove. And she fears if she doesn't remove them they'll just fall off into her clothes and onto everywhere she walks, sits and lays in bed.

They appear every time she goes number 1 except for roughly a day-long period immediately following going number 2, which suggests they're from any amount of fecal matter that's formed in her intestines.

These specks are so small that they are not visible to the naked eye unless you look really closely.

​

She spends about an hour in the bathroom every time she goes number 1, and at least 3 hours when she goes number 2, and 99% of both time periods is JUST so she can clean herself up after the actual deed.

It drains all her time and energy every single day. She's too exhausted to do anything other than sit on the couch and do stuff on the laptop.

This leaves me to have to keep on top of all the chores...and as you can imagine being one person dealing with chores generated from two people is not easy, especially when one of those people is generating way more than the normal amount of trash because of their health issues.

She's been to a few different doctors a number of times about her issues. They've done blood tests, put a camera up her rear and tested a fecal matter sample. Every single test revealed nothing abnormal.

The doctors are clueless. One even suggested it's all in her head and wanted to send her to a phsychiarist. No, it is NOT all in her head. These are real, physical symptoms she's having. I've seen the discharge myself on a number of occasions.

They also keep asking if it's diarrhea or constipation for some reason, but it's neither of those.

It's like they just don't understand what we're trying to tell them. We feel like we're not able to explain our issues to them properly so they can fully understand what's going on. It doesn't help that normal GP appointments only have a short period of allotted time to talk to the doctor in, so we can't get the full story out.

We're also concerned they think she's making all this up just to get out of having to find a job.

And because her issue takes up all her time and energy, we rarely have the chance to make regular appointments to talk to the doctor more and maybe try some other tests to see if they can finally determine what's going on.

​

We have a few theories as to what could be affecting her but they're just theories. We're obviously not medical experts or anything. I'll put them in order from most likely culprit to least;

**Theory 1) Irratable Bowel Syndrome.**

This was suggested to us by someone we confided with in real life who just so happened to have IBS themselves and recognised the symptoms.

At the time, the symptoms did seem to match up. The discharge, at the time my partner was feeling like she didn't get rid of everything every time she went number 2, stomach cramps...I don't remember what else...

Another thing that points towards IBS is that, before her health issues arose, my partner has actually had the discharge appear throughout her life on very rare occasions, only much smaller amounts which cleared away with normal toilet paper usage, which suggests some kind of genetic issue that we can put somewhere under the IBS umbrella.

However, we scoured the internet and asked around a little bit regarding IBS but could not for the life of us find any mention of the tiny fecal specks.

In fact, it's as if the tiny fecal specks symptom doesn't exist AT ALL in any known medical ailment. At least, not as far as we can find.

**Theory 2) Toilet usage issues messed up her digestive tract.**

When my partner and I first started living together, we spent over a year sharing a house and a single bathroom with two other people.

And just about any time my partner used the bathroom during this time, one or both of the other two other people would come to the bathroom, find it occupied, tut, sigh, and then go back from whence they came while they wait for it to be unoccupied again.

Hearing them tutting and sighing caused my partner to become self-concious about her toilet usage and it discouraged her from using the bathroom as often as she needed, especially for number 2s.

She ended up holding number 2s way longer than she should, making them build up into huge toilet-clogging monsters which only worsened the issue.

We think her holding her number 2s like this might have messed up her internal pipes somewhere somehow.

When they had a look in there with the camera, they didn't really go very deep from what I saw on the diagram they provided afterwards. The damage could be further up where the camera didn't see.

Either that or holding so much for so long reprogrammed her chute to behave in this abnormal way and re-educating it back to normal will be difficult.

The only issue with this explanation is when we moved out of the living situation with those other two people into a place of our own, for the first couple of weeks there my partner's number 2s were actually perfectly normal. No issues whatsoever. Then one day, she found the discharge on her underwear. And that's where it all started about 3 years ago.

**Theory 3) Fecal Impaction**

We recently found this when looking up the question of if it's possible for your bowel movements to damage your bowels, and a lot of the symptoms seemed to line up with what my partner's been experiencing.

It could very well explain the particles...a bit of number 2 constantly stuck at the end of the chute or something like that...it would make sense...right?

I don't know if that's something they would spot when they went in with the camera that time though...

**Theory 4) A drastic change in diet messed up her digestive tract.**

My partner is originally from Romania, where she enjoyed healthy homemade food served to her by her family for every meal on a daily basis and she very rarely had any fast food.

Before she came to England, she was warned by a friend of hers that had already visited a few times that we pretty much only had fast food in our supermarkets.

I guess she wasn't prepared for just how true that statement is. In an instant she went from a healthy nutritious diet of daily homemade meals to having what amounts to something outta McDonalds every lunch and dinner.

She has no idea where to even look for the healthier homemade stuff she used to have, and neither do I.

Like jeez, England, get your culinary stuff together. I was having this stuff my whole life and never realised it wasn't normal until my partner told me when we got together. Nobody said anything to me until then, not even my parents. Heck, my parents even FED me that stuff when I was younger.

What's more, anything healthier is pretty darn expensive for the amount you get.

Healthier foods seriously need to be made more readily available for cheaper. No question about it.

**Theory 5) Dehydration.**

We reckon my partner is not getting enough liquid into her system. She has told me on multiple occasions she feels she needs to drink more than she is doing.

This is confirmed by the fact her number 2s are often quite dark, which is a sign of lack of hydration.

Unfortunately there's another issue preventing her from trying to drink more.

As well as the fact that her main health issues are causing her to spend an hour in the toilet every time she goes number 1, she's also been getting an occasional occurrence of periods of time where she constantly feels the need to go number 1, even from literally the split second after she just finished going number 1. She does try to squeeze out whatever's in there, but nothing comes out, and she still feels the need to go.

So she ends up finishing with the toilet while feeling the need to go number 1, and then going about her day until she's sure she has some liquid in there again, rinse, and repeat.

This constant feeling of needing to go has lead her to...have accidents on multiple occasions, especially when she's trying to wake up in the morning.

Like, as soon as she gets out of bed she has to rush to the toilet. But sometimes she's not fast enough to avoid drenching her garments.

The cold seems to make it much, much worse as well. She's always had a cold sensitivity but once she got these health issues, her feeling cold causes her bladder to go crazy.

And when she goes number 2, at the same time she finds herself going number 1 three or four times in a row, and then two or three more times while she's cleaning up after.

We have no idea where her bladder is getting all this liquid from. We're pretty confident she's outputting way more liquid than she's drinking each day.

In fact she seems to need to go as soon as she drinks something, like the drink is just going right through her.

We do suspect a UTI is at play, possibly brought on by her main health issue somehow.

So with her going number 1 or feeling the need to go number 1 all the time, and having to spend an hour every time, being motivated to drink more is pretty darn difficult.

**Theory 6) Stress**

The health problem may have been started by stress. And then she's stressing about the health problem. Aaaand hello vicious cycle.

**Theory 7) She's doing something wrong with wiping herself.**

This is a theory she has but one that I feel makes no sense. She has this idea that somehow she's doing something wrong with how she's wiping with the toilet paper and that's what's bringing out the discharge and the particles.

I have no idea how you can even do something wrong. You wipe along your crack. That's pretty much it. How can you get that wrong? I dunno.

I think those are all the theories we've come up with so far. So yeah, we think the problem could be any one of those theories, or even a combination of them.

​

Moving on, I should mention my partner is a bit of a cleanliness freak. So much so she absolutely refuses to sit on the porcelean throne without covering it in clean toilet paper first. She's convinced it's always dirty, no matter how much it's actually cleaned.

But with her issue with number 1s she's always ending up needing to go really, really bad like she can't hold it another minute so she has no time to cover the seat with paper,

So instead she goes number 1 just crouching over the toilet. So she's also standing the whole 1 hour it takes her to use the bathroom.

She's not just cleaning her buttcrack and/or her peepee hole either, she also cleans her buttcheeks and all down her legs, because she's convinced she's got those particles I talked about earlier falling all over those areas every time she uses the bathroom.

I don't know if that's actually happening, since I can't exactly watch what's happening to her in the bathroom. (It's way too small for two people to occupy)

That's not to mention each time she goes number 1 the liquid trickles down her legs each time. Oh, and obviously if she has an accident she has to clean that off her legs.

I have to help out as well by bringing packs of wet wipes and handing her the wet wipes for her to use. She always ends up using up a whole pack for number 1 and several packs (varying from 4 up to 8, sometimes more, depending on how bad the discharge decides to be) for number 2.

Here's another thing, she has to use so much toilet paper that it doesn't even fit in the toilet bowl, she has to use trash bins. And we live in an apartment block with a trash chute that's only big enough to fit shopping carrier bag sized trash bags.

So we have to have two small trash bins in the bathroom for all the toilet paper and wet wipes she uses, and every time she uses the bathroom she fills them to overflowing and it sometimes falls off onto the floor, and then she stresses about it blowing dirt from the floor and the fallen trash onto her, so she ends up cleaning herself even more from that, creating even more trash to put on the already overflowing trash bins!

I have suggested a third bin to help alleviate things but she doesn't think there's enough space. Her feet sometimes accidentally kick the two that's there already as it is.

And that's just from going number one. When she goes number two, about halfway through the whole ordeal we actually have to take the time for her to empty the bins of the full bags, give them to me to dispose of, and then have me give her fresh empty bags to put in the bins, and then she proceeds to fill and overflow those too before she's finished!

And we have to use gloves for this. In fact we have to use gloves for pretty much everything when she goes number two, so I have to bring her gloves to use!

Mostly gloves for the wet wipes to wipe her crack with. She doesn't want to get naked fingers covered in ass discharge while she's cleaning, obviously.

Also when she goes number two, she HAS to change all her clothes to a clean set, no question. Again, with gloves.

Also she has to put two period pads onto her underwear to be able to cover all three..."exits", hoping they'll catch anything that might otherwise fall onto her clothes.

As you can imagine, all this toilet paper, wet wipes and period pads causes a serious drain on our already lacking funds...and obviously we can't get any jobs while we're dealing with these health issues.

Also, all this standing around in the bathroom causes a lot of leg and back pain and she never really has time to recover before she needs the bathroom again so it's just steadily getting worse and worse and causing more and more pain.

When she goes walking, she worries about when she walks normally, her period pads feel like they're moving side to side and uncovering her butt crack and letting particles got into her pants, so to keep them centered as much as possible she does this weird slow stiff walk that only causes even more pain.

Lately she's been complaining about not having the physical strength to continue cleaning herself whenever she's in the toilet. She's not just talking about each partcular time, either, she means in general she feels like the time she spends in the toilet is draining her physical strength more and more.

She says she feels like she's just going to collapse in the bathroom one day, a thing she really doesn't want to happen, especially during number 2, because the floor is not clean at all, it's likely got those particles all over it and more often than not there's a puddle in front of the toilet as well from her not being able to hold number 1, and she doesn't know how to clean herself up after that. Wet wipes won't be enough and she'll be at the point where just jumping in the shower will just not be physically possible.

What's more she could get seriously injured from the collapse, possibly even to a fatal degree if she hits her head on something hard and unforgiving.

In general she's in fear of her life, that something's just gonna give and she's just gonna die from all this strain her body's being put through, and we feel absolutely powerless to stop it from happening.

I really can't stress enough just how bad it is. She keeps talking about how she's losing her mind and how she can't keep going on like this and she keeps yelling at the universe to just fluffing kill her already if that's what all this is leading to.

She also gets upset that she feels she ruined my life by coming into it, and I have to reassure her that's not the case. (I ruined my life plenty already by being a lazy piece of whatever before I met her)

Sometimes she gets so upset she wants to go kill herself somehow, and I have to try and help calm her down. But it's getting harder and harder each time. One time recently she got so upset she stormed off right out of our apartment and made it down four floors of stairs before I could get her to stop and calm down.

So I guess my question is this;

What the heck health issue is plaguing my partner, and how do we effectively communicate to a doctor in real life what's going on?
Response: This sounds like an issue with being obsessed with cleanliness and not a gastrointestinal disorder.
