Title: Anatomy Screen Second Opinion After Infant Loss
Body:
Hello,

After a completely “normal” and “healthy” pregnancy, I delivered at 38w0d — a beautiful baby girl with a postnatal diagnosis of HLHS and a handful of other cardiac anomalies. Despite heroic efforts, she passed at 7 weeks of age. 

I am looking for a second opinion on my anatomy screen from when I was 20 weeks pregnant with her. Said screen was read as “normal” with a “four-chamber heart” visualized. 

Many of her doctors feel that HLHS should have been seen on the anatomy screen. I have asked 7 different doctors (OB and MFM) if they would be willing to independently review the anatomy screen, and no one has agreed to do it. Any ideas for resources? I am happy to pay any price.
Response:
I can't speak for the OB field, but in my specialty it is very unlikely that anyone would review this type of data just for peace of mind.  For one, it wouldn't inform any change in care at this point, and for two, the interpreter would be 'put on the hook' so to speak. 


At the end of the day every test has a false positive and false negative rate, though sadly it may have had dire consequences in this case.  If you ultimately decide you want this information to seek damages I imagine you would have to work through a law firm.

Title: I have a question about the rabies virus in humans.
Body:
22M, 5’9”, white, 174lbs, drink and smoke occasionally.

Here’s a weird one for you. At the end of last week I was bitten by a woodchuck while trying to remove it from inside a gas station (long story). I immediately went to the ER and received an immuno-globulin shot, a tetanus shot, and my first two doses of the rabies vaccine. I just got my second round of the vaccine today. I know rabies can be transmitted through saliva and that it progresses pretty slowly in the body, but I don’t know *when* rabies becomes present in saliva. Is it when symptoms start? I really don’t want to kill my girlfriend by accident.

There is also no indication the woodchuck had rabies, it just really didn’t want to stop eating the Reese’s cups in the gas station.

Title: Husband (48) frequently fainting, poor appetite, losing weight
Body:
My husband for the past year has been frequently fainting and just had one of these spells. I was alerted to it because I heard his his head hit the tile floor in our kitchen. This isn’t the first time he has been injured in one of these falls.

In addition to that his appetite has become increasingly poor. The only foods he can tolerate are rice milk, rice cereal and peanut butter toast. He has also lost a fair amount of weight (20 lbs in the last 6 months).

He has had a Colonoscopy/Endoscopy within the last several months that was clear. He was also tested for food sensitivities/allergies. He also has had blood work done and everything was good.

His health history has been good with the exception of a parasite he contracted approximately 6 years ago while traveling out of the country. This parasite put him in the ICU and almost killed him. Thankfully the ICU doctors were able to treat the parasite but he was left with holes in his intestines. He is unsure of type of parasite but is confident that he contracted it from water in Uzbekistan. After the parasite he was never able to fully gain all of the healthy weight he had pre-parasite.

All of the doctors he has seen are stumped. Right now it’s a wait and see but with the increasing fainting spells, losing weight and poor appetite we don’t know what to do. At this point I’m afraid to let him out of my sight for too long for fear that he’ll really hurt himself during one of these falls. 

Is there any advice on what this could be or what we should have him tested for?
Response: He needs a full blood work up, cardiac workup and an ultrasound or CT scan of his whole abdomen - some parasites (liver flukes, etc) over a period of years can travel to the liver causing anorexia, jaundice and so much more. Someone also mentioned Neurocysticercosis which are pork tapeworms that can live in the brain. These same tapeworms plus other roundworms can also go into the heart muscles. Better to rule out. I'm a doctor in a developing country & cases like this are common.

Title: [32M] Should I go against my doctors advice and start cholesterol medication. I need a 2nd opinion.
Body:

These are my most recent lab results. Note: They're probably 5-10% higher because this was ~10 months ago.

Total Choleseterol 266
LDLs 207
HDLs 46
Triglycerides 67

Everything else in my blood work is normal. I've talked to my doctor about this 2 or 3 times now and every time he says "This has to be genetic, even with perfect dieting you could probably only swing the numbers by 5%, I feel unconfortable putting you on cholesterol medication because my youngest taking them is 38. There is not enough research to back up putting a 30 year old on statins."

All of that is reasonable and I agree with it. But I'm 32 and my cholesterol is a disaster. 0 people in my family or extended family have a cholesterol problem and frankly its really scary. I only cook with health oils. Home cooking 3-5 nights a week on average. I eat fast food maybe twice a month unless I'm on travel. I just want to know what other health professionals would recommend. 

Thanks for taking the time and helping.
Response:
Actually there is enough research. Tell him to get on the ASCVD guidelines and see that anyone with >190 LDL needs to be on a statin. 

Be on a statin.

Title: I took four doses of the Pfizer vaccine. Am I in danger?
Body:
Hello. I am a 28 year old male who just today took his fourth shot of the Pfizer vaccine. Long story short, I moved from my home country to an EU country last month, and this particular EU country does not acknowledge my home country as a vaccinating country, meaning the two Pfizer doses I took in my home country are for naught. Taking an antibodies test was an option, but it was an expensive one, and they only give out *temporary* immunity cards, which need to be renewed every couple of months by taking yet another antibodies test.

I do know that Pfizer now recommends 3rd booster shots, which was my original plan when I took my first dose in EU (3rd in total), but then I was afraid that they will enforce restrictions in the future for people who only took one dose, so I decided to take my 2nd dose in EU (4th in total).

My question now is: am I in any immediate or eventual danger? Keep in mind that I have had very mild-to-non-existent side-effects to all first three doses; just a slight pain in my left arm where I took the shots. So far I feel fine after the fourth one which I took today morning, but I believe it's too early to tell now.
Response: You should be fine.
